Reference guide

Start

How a Scena script starts — the import, the window, the game loop — and the rules and words the rest of the Guide uses.

Minimal script / init → Minimal script
Coming from Scratch, Unity or Pygame → From another engine
Rules → Rules
Units, Entity, point, frame… → Vocabulary
PNG / SVG file → Image files
st / canvas / clock… → Global singletons
setup / update / on_key → Script callbacks
Formula, check, event or process? → Which to use

The Guide's examples assume from scena import * and init(…) at the start and run() at the end. from scena import * is the only import: everything the Guide shows comes from it.

From another engine

The Scratch, Unity, Godot or Pygame way, and the Scena way. The idea is the same; the spelling changes.

You would writeIn Scena
“forever” (Scratch), while running: with pygame.event.get()def update(dt): runs every frame; Scena runs the loop. A while inside update freezes the window: use if. A sequence with waits is a task (async def + await wait(1), with run_task)
“wait 1 seconds”, time.sleep(1)after(1, f); in a task, await wait(1). time.sleep stops the whole game
clock.tick(60)Not needed: update(dt) receives the frame's time. The rate is canvas.framerate = 60
Update() / FixedUpdate() in a classon_update(self, dt)
Start() / Awake()setup(self)
Godot: _process(delta), _ready(), queue_free()on_update(self, dt), setup(self), self.destroy(). A child that moves with its parent: child["center"] @= lambda: parent.center + Vec2(20, 0)
OnTriggerEnter2D(other), OnCollisionEnter2D, rect.colliderect(other) every frameon_collide(self, other) in the class, or @collide("hero", "coin"): runs when they start touching. To ask right now: test_collision(a, b)
OnMouseDown(), “when this sprite clicked”on_click(self), or @click(obj). A click anywhere: def on_mouse_click(x, y, button): at the top of the file
Destroy(obj, 0.4), “delete this clone”obj.destroy(); after a while, after(0.4, obj.destroy)
transform.position, transform.rotation.center (move it with move_to / move_by), .angle, .scale
“hide” / “show”, SetActive(false)visible = False / True hides only the drawing (it still collides); active = False stops everything
“glide 1 secs to x: y:”move_to(x, y, time=1) (the time goes by name)
“point towards”obj.rotate_to(heading(obj, target))
“broadcast message” / “when I receive”Call the function. Or count: st.waves += 1 with @on_change(st["waves"]), which compares once per frame (two writes that go back to the old value in the same frame do not fire it)
“create clone of myself”obj.clone(); see what the copy takes along in the clone table
x += vel * dtWorks: obj.move_by(obj.vel.x * dt, obj.vel.y * dt) in update (or on_update). Scena does not move anything by its vel on its own; vel is the velocity that bounce= reads and rewrites
self.vel = 200 (the speed, a number)vel is every object's 2D velocity (self.vel = (200, 0)), the one resolve(…, bounce=) uses; you do the moving, with move_by(vel.x * dt, vel.y * dt). A number of your own needs another name: self.speed = 200
cooldown -= dt … if cooldown <= 0: cooldown = 0.6Works, but it throws away whatever went past zero, and the rhythm changes with the frame rate. @every(0.6) or ready("shot", 0.6) keep the remainder

Minimal script

Every script has three parts. from scena import * and init(…) set up the game's space. The body of the file creates the objects — each constructor already puts its object on the screen. run() opens the window and runs the game, calling update(dt) every frame.

from scena import *
init(width=1200, height=800)

SkyGradient("night")
Stars()
Vignette()
t = Triangle(center=(400, 300), radius=50, color="cyan")

def update(dt):
    t.rotate_by(30 * dt)

run()
init

init(width=2000, height=1200, title="Scena", window_scale=0.8, display="windowed", ui_scale=, ui_font=)

Sets up the design space and the window; it does not open the window (run() does). It already runs on its own at import scena, with the defaults. Call it again right after from scena import * if the script reads canvas.width / .height before run(). run() takes no size.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
widthname=number2000Width of the design space (canvas.width). Not the OS window in pixels.
heightname=number1200Height of the design space (canvas.height). y-up, origin at the bottom-left corner.
titlename=str"Scena"The OS window's title.
window_scalename=number0.8Fraction of the largest windowed window that fits the desktop (the design's aspect, decorations on, taskbar visible). 1.0 = as large as the area allows. 0.8 = 80% of that, centered. Startup only: used up when the window opens. There is no canvas.window_scale.
displayname=str"windowed"Shortcut for canvas.display. Only "windowed" · "maximized" · "fullscreen". The windowed window is created first (scale, centered); then it switches to the mode.
ui_scalename=numbercurrentWrites ui.scale. Leaving it out keeps the current value (import default: 1).
ui_fontname=strcurrentWrites ui.font (a family, or a .ttf / .otf file). Leaving it out keeps the current value.

The OS window follows from the design's aspect, the monitor's desktop area, the window's real borders and window_scale. It always starts centered. There is no x= / y= / window_width= in pixels — drag the window if you need a specific spot.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
init(width=, height=) is the OS window's sizethe design space. The windowed window fits the desktop with the same aspect; window_scale=1 is the largest windowed fit. display="maximized" fills the area (black bars). display="fullscreen" covers the monitor.canvas.window_scale

Rules

Five rules that hold everywhere in Scena.

  1. A constructor places. Circle() shows up right away. So do Rain(), Vignette(), Slider().
  2. Materials and effects only show up applied to an object (or to the background). Gradient, Color, Blur, Neon, Sheet draw nothing on their own: they go in .fill, .visual, set_color, Sprite(sheet) or canvas.background.
  3. = copies now. @= links live. c.radius = 10 · c["radius"] @= lambda: player.hp * 10 — see Reactive.
  4. A property is state. A method is an action. c.visible = False · c.move_by(20, 0)
  5. Sizes in design units, y up, angles in degrees. The origin is the bottom-left corner; 0° points right. See units. Widgets are pinned to the window and ignore the camera.

Each parameter table explains itself: common parameters (layer=, group=, a widget's 1st argument) appear again in every table, so you never have to jump to another section.

Vocabulary

The words the Guide always uses in the same sense. When a section says “units”, “point”, “Graphic” or “frame”, this is what it means.

TermWhat it is
design unit (“units”)The measure of everything in Scena: position, size, radius, thickness, speed (units per second). The space runs from 0 to the width and from 0 to the height given to init: with init(width=2000, height=1200), the center of the screen is (1000, 600). The window scales that whole space to fit the monitor, so 1 unit is not 1 pixel — the game looks the same on any screen. y grows upward; (0, 0) is the bottom-left corner; angles are in degrees, 0 = to the right, counterclockwise.
frameOne turn of the game: read the keyboard and mouse, run update(dt) and the on_updates, move, collide, draw. About 60 per second. dt is how many seconds have passed since the previous frame — multiply speeds by it (200 * dt = 200 units per second).
EntityEvery game object: Shape, Sprite, Text, SpatialFx, widgets and the Entity() with no drawing. Every Entity can have its own fields (ship.hp), timers (after / every), a mode, groups and destroy().
GraphicAn Entity with a drawn body and a pose: Shape, Sprite (and Svg) and Text. Only a Graphic can be clicked or dragged, travel with move_to and have a .box. SpatialFx and widgets are not Graphics.
poseWhere the object is and which way it faces: center, angle, scale and the mirror (flip_x / flip_y). The verbs in Move change the pose; color and visual are not part of it.
ShapeA geometric Graphic: Circle, Rect, Square, Concave, Line, Ellipse, Polygon, RegularPolygon, Triangle, Point, Track.
pointWherever the API asks for a place (move_to, center=, about=, query_point…), any of these works: a tuple (x, y), a Point, a Vec2, a Graphic (its center counts) or mouse. The position is copied at that instant; to follow it, use lambda: (Reactive). More in Points.
field / AttributeA value Scena keeps track of: st.score, ship.hp, c.radius. When it changes, whatever depends on it (an @= formula, an @when, a widget) finds out. Attribute is the name of the class behind it.
link (@=)Make a field follow a formula: c["radius"] @= lambda: ship.hp works it out again whenever ship.hp changes. The opposite of =, which copies the value once.
HandleThe object that verbs which take time return (after, tween, move_to(…, time=) or speed=, play_sound…): use it to cancel, pause or wait for that task. See Handle.
modeThe chapter of behavior an Entity is in right now (e.mode = e.diving). What it starts (timers, movements) stops when it ends. See Mode.
stageThe top of the file: what it creates (objects, timers, sounds, layers) lasts the whole game and works in every act. What an act creates leaves with it. See The stage and the act.
slot (name=)A name that holds a single task: after(2, hint, name="hint") called again with the same name replaces the previous one instead of adding another. A slot belongs to a place: the object of the call (ship.after(…, name=)); for a bare call, whoever is in the running mode (inside a mode's body, an act's mode included); outside a mode (the top of the script, an act's setup, callbacks), the game / the current act. The same name in two places is two slots: a bare play_sound(…, name="music") in an act's setup and another bare one in the act's mode play together. For a single task, always call from the same place — an act's soundtrack with self.play_sound(…, name="music"), which is the same slot as a bare call in the act's mode. A timer or sound of the stage (the top of the script) whose name the act reuses, from any of those places, is paused during the act and comes back after the change: the stage's soundtrack does not play along with the act's. A stage task does not pause: its name in a bare call in the act is an error.
a world with a floorA game with gravity (platformer, runner) writes collision.floor = True: whatever rests on something below stands on it (it doesn't slide down the ramp, it rides along with the elevator). Without that line, the default, no side is special: a game seen from above, in space or without gravity. See A world with a floor.
place × travelPlacing puts the object straight in its spot (center = …, move_to without time=) and goes through walls. Traveling moves it there (move_by, move_to(…, time=) or speed=, move_along), and a resolve() wall stops it midway; the @collide of a fast traveler checks the whole path (Fast objects). Turning in place and scaling (rotate_* / scale_*) are never stopped by a wall: it only pushes the object out afterward. Turning around another point (rotate_by(…, about=)) carries the center along, and that is traveling.
held × on the frame it is pressedkeyp("A") is True on every frame the key is held; keyp.once("A") only on the frame it was pressed. @when fires when the condition turns from False to True, not while it stays True.
channelIn Transients, the place of one kind of effect: a new flash replaces the running flash, but lives alongside a pop.
HUDText and controls pinned to the window (score, lives, menus), on the "ui" layer: they don't move with the camera.

Image files

Where Scena looks for the image files (PNG, JPG, SVG and XML / JSON atlases) you pass by name: next to the script or in its media/ folder.

Sprite, Sheet, Svg, Texture and Wallpaper use the same search. The name is used as given — the framework does not look into subfolders on its own.

  1. An absolute path. Only that file. It exists or it is missing.
  2. The script's folder. Next to the .py you ran.
  3. media/ next to the script. Sprite("ship.png") finds media/ship.png.
  4. The folder you ran Python from. The cwd. Last resort. 
Sprite("ship.png")
Sprite("sprites/ship.png")   # media/sprites/ship.png next to the script
Texture("floor.png")
Wallpaper("sky.jpg")

A missing file does not stop the game: a checkerboard shows in place of the image, with a warning, and the object works normally. In the REPL or with python -c, the search starts in the current folder. Atlases: the PNG sits next to the XML / JSON that describes it. A pattern with * (Sheet and strip, File patterns) searches the same folders and uses only the first one that has a matching file.

Global singletons

These objects already exist after from scena import * — you don't build them, you just use them. The classes, functions and effects come with the same import; the search box at the top of the page indexes all of them.

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
stStateread / writeYour game's values (score, lives, level), tracked by Scena. Keeping values.
canvasCanvasread / writeThe screen: camera, background, full-screen effects, layers. World.
clockClockread / writeGame time: dt, time, pause and slow motion. clock.
keypKeyPressedreadKeyboard: which key is held, which one was just pressed. Keyboard.
mouseMousereadPointer: position in the world, and buttons. Mouse.
audiomixerread / writeSound as a whole: master volume, mute, meters. audio.
uistackread / writeThe widgets' size and font, and the column they stack in. UI.
groupgroupsread / writeFinds objects by tag: group["enemy"]. Groups.
collisionqueriesread / writeCollision questions (what is at this point?) and drawing the colliders. Collision.

Script callbacks

Functions with fixed names that you write in the script and run() calls at the right moment: setup once, when the window opens; update every frame; on_key_down when a key is pressed; and so on. The full table is in Script callbacks.

def setup(canvas):
    canvas.fx_quality = "high"

def update(dt, canvas):
    if keyp("RIGHT"):
        player.move_by(200 * dt, 0)

def on_key_down(key):
    if key == "ESC":
        canvas.reset_view()

def on_mouse_scroll(xoffset, yoffset):
    factor = 1.1 if yoffset > 0 else 1 / 1.1
    canvas.zoom_by(factor, about=(mouse.x, mouse.y))

Each function asks only for the parameters it wants: Scena passes the ones it declares. update(dt) and update(dt, canvas) both work. Catalog: Script callbacks and Entity callbacks.

Which to use

Your code runs in three ways: a formula stays true, a check is made every frame, an event runs once, at one instant. What takes time is a process, and every process has an owner. Choose by what the game needs: none of them is just for beginners, and a big game uses them all.

I wantI use
something to always match something else (the lamp's color)a formula: lambda, @=
to know a state every frame (is the key held?)a check in update or in on_update
to react to an instant (a key, a click, a hit, leaving the screen)an event: on_key_down, on_click, @collide, @leave_playfield
to react when a condition becomes true@when
once, laterafter
again and againevery
a sequence with waits, for what the object is doingan async mode
one more sequence, or one that belongs to no objectrun_task

Check or event. For a state (is the key held?), the check; for an instant (the key just went down), the event. A flash inside if keyp("SPACE") restarts on every frame the key is held.

Processes. after, every, a movement with time=, a sound, a sequence: they all return the same Handle. One thing at the end of a process: then= / on_done=. Two waits or more: an async function — a mode, when it is what the object is doing (one at a time), or a task, when it runs alongside or belongs to no object.

Owner. A process's owner is the place where it started — the game or the act, an object, a mode — and the process ends when its owner ends: changing mode cancels what the old mode started. See scope and cancelling.

Where else to look — Reactive · Draw · Frame · Script callbacks

Draw

The objects that appear on screen: geometric shapes (Shapes), images (Sprite), curves (Track), text (Text) and effects in the world (SpatialFx). Each constructor already puts the object on screen. To lay out a fleet or a grid: Place. To move and animate: Move.

Circle / Rect / Line… → Shapes
Image / atlas → Sprite
Curve → Track
Text → Text
Fire / rain in the world → SpatialFx
Object with no drawing → Entity

Every object on screen

What holds for every object that appears on screen — Shape, Sprite, Text and SpatialFx: hiding, parking, destroying, layer, group and .center. It is written here once; the section for each type does not repeat it.

ship.visible = False
# park: it disappears, timers and collision stop
# (a sound from the ship keeps playing; its on_done waits for the ship to come back)
ship.active = False
# cancels timers/tweens/mode; the Entity stays alive
ship.cancel_process()
# gone for good. is_alive becomes False
ship.destroy()
Constructor (every object on screen)

A name with =: pass it by name. Works on Shape, Sprite and SpatialFx.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
layer=name=str, int or None"default"Drawing layer. A number = a position (created on the spot). None = outside the list.
group=name=str or list or NoneA tag, or a list of tags. E.g. group="wasp".
 
ship = Sprite("ship.png", layer="ui", group=["wasp", "enemy"])
# ship: the variable is how you find this object later.
# layer: drawn on the "ui" layer (outside the world's normal order).
# group: joins group["wasp"] and group["enemy"] at the same time.

There is no id= and no lookup by name: keep the object in a variable. To find it where the variable does not reach (another function, another class), give it a tag and read the group: Sprite("hero.png", group="hero") … group["hero"].first.

On every object on screen

Properties

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.centerpoint(400, 300)read / writeThe object's center: the point that move_to puts in place and that it turns around. Every object on screen has one. On a Point, it is the Point itself (p.center is p).
visibleboolFalseread / writeHides the drawing. It stays on its layer.
activeboolFalseread / writeParks: hides, removes collision, pauses timers and on_update. The parts go along: the markers from show_handles() disappear and do not drag until it comes back. Prefer it to destroying and re-creating.
is_aliveboolTruereadTrue until destroy(). if ship: is the same test. Independent of visible. The parts (ship.center, seg.p1) die with it: they can still be read, but changing them raises an error.
.layerstr, int or None"default"read / writeCurrent layer. Write it to change it (a number creates the layer on the spot).
time_scalenumber1read / writeAn extra multiplier on this Entity (timers, tweens, wait, on_update). Default 1. See clock.

Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
destroy()No parameters—Takes the object out of the game: it disappears and stops colliding. Cancels its timers, tweens and mode, and the quick effects under way (without calling on_done). On a part (c.center) it raises TypeError: a part lives, parks and dies with its owner.
cancel_process()No parametersselfCancels this Entity's timers / tweens / sounds / mode; it stays alive. Does not fire on_destroy or @exit_mode. See scope.
move_to_front() / move_to_back()No parameters—Drawing order within the layer. top still stays above default. Not on SpatialFx.
tag / untag / taggedParameters: names (names); tagged takes name (name)tag/untag return nothing; tagged returns True/Falsetag puts the object in groups, untag takes it out, tagged("x") says whether it is in group "x". The same names as in collision and group["wasp"]. A part of the shape (c.center, seg.p1, a vertex) has no tags: tag on it raises TypeError — tag the owner.
on_updateParameters: e (object), dt (number)—fn(e, dt) every frame, even during await. See Frame.
on_destroyParameters: e (object)—Once, from inside destroy().
setup(self)Parameters: self (this object)—A method you write in a subclass; Scena calls it right after the constructor. It is not the script's setup(canvas).
clone(center=, scale=, layer=, group=)Parameters: center (point, optional), scale (number), layer (str), group (str or list)the copied objectA copy. center= puts the copy at that point (omitted: where the original is). Runs setup(). No timers / mode / click callbacks. Not on SpatialFx. Clone.
look_like(other)Parameters: other (another object)—Copies another object's look (color, outline, visual, add-ons). Not on SpatialFx.
prepare_fx(*visuals)Parameters: visuals (Visual)—Computes the Sprite's silhouette for those visuals ahead of time (avoids a hitch on the first switch). Does nothing on Shape / Entity.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
Hiding = removingvisible=False hides, and the object stays. destroy() removes — the Python reference remains, but if ship: becomes false. ship.move_by after that raises DestroyedError (the message says where the destroy() happened). .center still reads.a live object
ship.enabled = FalseAttributeError. Parking is ship.active = False. .enabled exists elsewhere, with another meaning: on a widget, it shows it disabled (dimmed, not responding); on a Post, a background or a sound effect, it turns that effect on and off.the same as .active

Shapes

Shapes are the geometric forms: circle, rectangle, line, ellipse, polygon, point. They appear as soon as they are created; with no arguments (Circle()) they start at a medium size in the middle of the world, (width / 2, height / 2) of init — the middle of the screen while the camera has not moved; after a pan_to or set_origin("center"), pass center=. All of them take color=, visual=, line_width=, layer= and group=.

c = Circle(center=(400, 300), radius=50, color="cyan")
c.set_color("tomato")
c.visual = Neon()
c.show_handles()
Constructor (every Shape)

Every Shape (Circle, Rect, Line, Polygon…) takes these, besides layer= and group= (Every object on screen):

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
color=name=color"cyan"Paints the inside and an outline in a contrasting tone. On Line, it paints the stroke. Omitted: the default color (set_defaults).
visual=name=VisualNeon()Starts with that visual — the same as c.visual = Neon() afterwards. Use color= or visual=, not both.
line_width=name=number1.5Thickness of the outline (on Line, of the stroke), in design units. Change it later with .line_width.

Defaults for the next shapes

set_defaults(…) chooses the look of the Shapes created after the call — so you do not repeat color= / visual= on each one. Those already created do not change. It lasts until the next call; in an act, an act change goes back to what the top of the file left.

set_defaults(visual=Neon())
set_defaults("coral", line_width=2.0, dash="dot")

set_defaults(visual=None, line_width=, dash=, line_cap=, line_join=, line=, fill=, blend=, line_filter=, fill_filter=)

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
visual1stcolor, Gradient, Texture or Visual"coral"The basic look: a color ("coral"), a Gradient / Texture or a visual (Neon()).
line_width · dash · line_cap · line_joinname=number / str2.0 / "dot"The outline: thickness, dash pattern, ends and corners — the same values as the properties in Shape reference.
fill · linename=color, Gradient or TextureMaterial of the inside / of the outline, like .fill / .line.
blendname=str"add"How they mix with what is already drawn. See Blend.
fill_filter · line_filtername=filterBlur(sigma=2)Pixel filter on the inside / on the outline. See Filters.
Shape reference

Properties

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.colorcolor"cyan"read / writePrimary solid color: the fill on area shapes, the stroke on Line. Writing it calls set_color. It reads the current color: with a visual, that is the color the visual paints now, which may not be the one you gave — a Halo makes the body translucent, lighter or darker (alpha included), so c.color = "red" followed by c.color reads that tone. A visual that paints its own material or its own palette (Flame, Swell, Water, Metal(), Shield()) has no single color: there .color reads the color you gave. To keep your color, store it in a variable or in st.
.visualVisual or NoneNeon()read / writeThe main visual (one per object). None removes the visual; add-ons stay.
.glow / .shadow / .tailbool or color or GlowTrueread / writeAdd-ons. Sprite also has .hue and .gray. Shortcut: True / color / number / object. Reading returns the settings object (Glow, Shadow…) or None.
.fill / .linecolor or GradientGradient("sunset")read / writeThe material of the inside (.fill) or of the outline (.line): a color, a Gradient or a Texture. A Gradient only shows when you put it here. With a visual on, the visual follows the new value (an outline visual follows .line; a body visual, .fill): writing before or after setting the visual gives the same result.
.blendstr"add"read / writeHow fill and line mix with the canvas. Default "normal". With a visual on, it works like .line_width: a visual that fixes its own blend (Halo adds light) keeps it. Blend.
.line_widthnumber1.5read / writeStroke thickness. Default 1.5 (Shape). Also a constructor keyword on the shapes that draw a stroke. Point and Anchor refuse it. It stays writable afterwards. With a visual on, it gives the same as writing it before setting the visual: a visual that uses the thickness (Neon, Laser…) follows the new value; one that fixes its own (Rim, Halo, Shield…) keeps it, and the value shows with visual = None. Text has its own.
.dashstr"dash"read / writeStroke pattern. Default "solid". "solid" · "dash" · "dot" · "dot-dash". With a visual on, like .line_width.
.line_capstr"round"read / writeThe stroke's ends. Default "round" (rounded). "butt": flat, stops at the end point. "square": flat, half the line width past the end point. ("project", the old name of "butt", raises TypeError with the fix.)
.line_joinstr"miter"read / writeThe stroke's corners. Default "miter". "miter" · "bevel" · "round".
.is_collapsedboolFalsereadRead-only. True if the extent has no inside (an axis at 0 / radius=0 / length=0). It is not fill or visible. Silent — no warning. Point / Track / free polygon: always False.

Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
set_color(…)Parameters: colors (name, Color or RGB; positional)—Changes the object's color: inside, outline and the visual — the same as color= in the constructor, with or without a visual (the outline is derived from the color, and an outline visual follows that outline). Every visual that takes color= shows the new color: a visual created with a color (Neon("red"), Laser("blue"), Rim("gold")…) starts following the object, Metal() becomes metal of the new color. A visual without color= (Flame, Water, Shield(style="nebula")…) keeps the color and warns: it shows when the visual is removed. The same color forms.
show_handles() / no_handles() / show_points()No parameters—show_handles() shows draggable markers on the points that define the shape (center, ends, vertices), so you can adjust it with the mouse; no_handles() hides them. show_points() shows every point, just to look. The markers go away with the shape on destroy().
clone(center=, scale=, layer=, group=)Parameters: center (point, optional), scale (number), layer (str), group (str or list)the copied objectA free copy (the geometry is copied now, with no links). center= moves the copy to that point (the geometric center lands there, as with move_to); a function raises TypeError (link it afterwards: dup.center @= …). It does not inherit timers or mode. frame= is Sprite-only.
look_like(other)Parameters: other (another object)—Copies another object's look (color, outline, visual, add-ons).
save_visual() / restore_visual()No parameters—Remembers the current look (add-ons included) and goes back to it later (it keeps a single look). A second save_visual does nothing until restore_visual. Different from .visual = None (removes the visual; add-ons stay).

An incomplete construction model (Circle(p1=…) without p2) raises ValueError. It does not fall back to the default.

A filled circle — or a slice of one, with angle= / spread=. Circle() already appears in the middle. Also Circle.from_points, Circle.from_corners and tangent_lines_from.

c = Circle(center=(400, 300), radius=50, color="cyan")
c = Circle(center=(400, 300), radius=50)
Circle(p1=(100, 200), p2=(300, 200))   # diameter
p = c.point_at_angle(45)               # throwaway Point on the edge
dots = Track(c).spaced_points(8)       # 8 (x, y) tuples on the outline
c = Circle(center=(400, 300), radius=50, color="cyan")
c.set_color("tomato")
c.visual = Neon()
c.move_by(200 * dt, 0)
c.move_by(angle=90, distance=40)
c.move_by(distance=120 * dt)
c.rotate_by(30 * dt)

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
corner_radius changes the collisionClicks follow the rounded corner. Collision stays the rectangle. Linked corners stay alive. corner_radius is a plain number — a function raises an error.—
angle= with p1=, p2= turns the boxangle= tilts the box with the corners pinned and changes its size. To turn a rectangle of fixed size, use center= + angle=, or rotate_by.—
.top_right is always the top-right cornerIt is the corner that was there on first use, and the name follows that point. Drag p1 past p2 and top_right is still p2, even at the bottom left — whatever is linked to top_right never jumps to another point. The .box keeps the same names. For the screen, use the edges: rect.box.top / .right.A name recomputed every frame
flip_x on a Rect turns the boxIt mirrors: each named point goes to its mirror image around the center (top_left ends up where top_right was). The box does not move.A half turn

Writing a derived point. The midpoints of the sides (.top_center, .left_center…) and the centers of the end squares are read-only: to change them, change width / height / center. To move the rectangle until one of them sits at a given place: r.move_to(1, 2, about=r.top_center).

p1=, p2=, height=, anchor=. The orientation comes from p1→p2; height is the thickness (≥ 0); .width becomes the length along the axis. anchor is required: "cap" (midpoints of the short walls = .left_center/.right_center), "square" (centers of the squares of side height = .left_square_center/.right_square_center), "side_left" / "side_right" (corners of a long side; the box sits to the left or to the right of p1→p2). These derived points exist in every model, not only in the p1=, p2=, height=, anchor= model.

An isosceles triangle: two equal sides (side) and the base, opposite the apex, base_ratio times that length. Without base_ratio it is equilateral (three equal sides). angle is where the tip (the apex) points, as with every heading: 0 to the right, 90 straight up. Good for ships and arrows: you can see it turn.

Triangle()
Triangle(center=(400, 300), radius=50, color="cyan")
ship = Triangle(center=(400, 300), radius=30, angle=90, base_ratio=0.6)
t.rotate_by(30 * dt)

A name with =: pass it by name.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
centername=pointdesign centerPoint
radiusname=numbermedium sizeDistance from the center to the apex. The center is the centroid (the balance point). On the equilateral triangle, it is the circumradius.
sidename=number60Or the size by the two equal sides, instead of radius=.
vertexname=point(0, 0)With side=: places the triangle by its apex instead of its center.

Changing it later keeps what placed the triangle: with radius, the center and the apex; with side, the equal sides. It links with @= and animates with tween.

With base_ratio=: the largest triangle with that ratio that fits, centered. With radius= / side=: only centers. With a formula (box=lambda: …), it follows the region. box=.

Do not pass n=: it is always 3 (TypeError). Three free corners: Polygon(points=[…]). EquilateralTriangle became Triangle in 0.9.0 (the old name raises TypeError with the fix).

A box with a scoop (scoop): a piece of a circle or of an ellipse cut out of it. A quarter-pipe, the curved corner of a pinball table, the inside curve of a track, a half-pipe. You place it like a Rect (every model, the named points, angle); the curve comes from the box.

Concave()
ramp = Concave(top_left=(0, 200), width=200, height=200)           # quarter-pipe
nook = Concave(top_left=(0, 600), width=80, height=80, scoop="bottom_right")
halfpipe = Concave(center=(400, 100), width=400, height=250,
                   scoop="top_center", rim=(0, 50))                # a floor of 50
deck = Concave(top_left=(0, 200), width=200, height=200, rim=(20, 0))

A corner ("top_left", "top_right", "bottom_left", "bottom_right") cuts out a quarter; the midpoint of a side ("top_center", "bottom_center", "left_center", "right_center") cuts out half an ellipse — a semicircle when the box is 2:1. Locked at construction.
rimname=number or pair0The solid left at the ends of the curve, along the width and the height: rim=0 leaves the ends knife-thin; rim=(20, 0) gives the quarter-pipe a deck of 20 at the top and no step at the floor. The curve's radius on each axis is the box's reach minus the rim. ≥ 0 (negative: ValueError). It links with @=; scale_by scales it.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
A Concave is a RectIt uses the same frame, but it does not collide as a box: it is solid up to the curve. isinstance(c, Rect) is False. Rounded (convex) corners are Rect(corner_radius=); Concave has no corner_radius.—
Collision follows the drawn curveAlmost: the curve is drawn as a true arc and collides as chords at most 0.25 units from it (like the Circle pie slice). The chord ends lie on the curve: a ball stops up to 0.25 short of the drawn curve, never past it. Clicks (contains_point) follow the exact curve; a point right on the curve counts as inside. A ball rolls up the ramp and comes back.A box
scoop changes laterIt is locked at construction, like RegularPolygon's n. To mirror it: flip_x / flip_y. The rim changes freely.—

A Point is an (x, y) position that lives in the game: it can be linked, dragged and used by other objects (the end of a Line, the center of a Circle). Invisible by default; color= shows it as a marker and handle=True makes it draggable (both move it to the top layer).

p = Point(200, 150)
p = Point(200, 150, color="cyan")   # visible guide (not draggable)
p = Point(canvas.game_view.center)  # a copy of the view's center
p.visible = True
p.handle = True
# visible + draggable Point on top
a = Anchor(400, 300)
b = Anchor(500, 300, color="lime")

== on a Point compares the object, not the position. elevator.center == (400, 120) is always False, even with the elevator there; the same goes for a Vec2 and for another Point at the same place. Scena warns in the console (a Python warning pointing at your line). To test the position: distance(elevator.center, (400, 120)) == 0 (or < 1 if the movement does not land exactly). To know whether it is the same object: a is b.

Anchor

A shortcut: a Point that is visible and draggable on top, always: a.draggable = False (or handle = False) raises TypeError — for a point the mouse does not move, use Point(x, y, visible=True). No incoming link: a["field"] @= … raises LinkedAttributeError. It takes the same points as Point(point) (a copy). color= paints the marker (omitted: automatic red).

a = Anchor(400, 300)
a = Anchor(400, 300, color="cyan")
a = Anchor(canvas.game_view.center)
b = Anchor(600, 300)
Line(p1=lambda: a.center, p2=lambda: b.center)   # follows the drag

Linking to an Anchor takes a lambda. Line(p1=a.center, …) (or p1=a) copies the position once: the line stays where it started when the Anchor is dragged. To follow it: p1=lambda: a.center (Formulas in constructors).

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
Point(canvas.game_view.center) follows the viewIt copies the position once (game_view is a new Box on every read). To follow it: Point(lambda: canvas.game_view.center) or @=. A single lambda links the whole Point; for one axis only: Point(lambda: mouse.x, 0).a link
Point(…, color=…) can be draggedcolor= only shows the marker. To drag: p.handle = True or Anchor(…). All of a shape's points: shape.show_handles().handle
p.handle()handle is a property: p.handle = True.a method
x, y = ship.center follows the shipTwo numbers from now (a copy). To follow it, read ship.center.x where you need it or link with @= / lambda.a link

Sprite

A Sprite is an image on the screen — a still PNG or an animation. The Sprite is the object (position, size, rotation, collision); the Sheet is the catalog of frames and animations (clips) it takes its image from, and a Sheet never appears on its own. A still PNG needs no Sheet. Here “frame” also means each frame of the animation (frame= picks one); “every frame” still means each pass of the game loop.

# A still PNG: no Sheet.
potion = Sprite("potion.png", height=48, center=(200, 300))

# A PNG laid out as a grid, with one animation: fps= on the Sheet registers the clip, and the Sprite plays it right away.
snail = Sheet("snail.png", cols=8, fps=6)
Sprite(snail, height=36, center=(400, 300))

# Several clips: the Sheet names them, the Sprite picks one with play.
hero_sheet = Sheet("hero.png", cols=4, rows=3)
hero_sheet.clip("walk", [3, 4, 5, 6], fps=12)
hero_sheet.clip("jump", [7, 8, 9], fps=10)
hero = Sprite(hero_sheet, height=64, center=(600, 300))
hero.play("walk")

# One PNG per frame: a * where the name changes picks them all,
# in order (Idle__000.png, Idle__001.png, …).
ninja = Sheet(anchor="bottom", pixel_size=0.16)
ninja.strip("idle", "ninja/Idle__*.png", fps=8)
ninja.strip("running", "ninja/Run__*.png", fps=12)
fighter = Sprite(ninja, center=(800, 300))
fighter.play("running")
TypeRoleGoes into the game?
SheetCatalog: the pixels, how to cut them (grid, atlas, several files) and the named clips (clip, strip).No. It goes in Sprite(sheet). One Sheet serves many Sprites.
SpriteThe object on the screen: position, size, which frame / clip plays (play), facing and collision (hitbox).Yes, in the constructor. File: lookup. Missing: a checkerboard + a warning, and the Sprite carries on.

I have these files → Loading sprites
Clips, play, different sizes per clip → Animating sprites
Turn, aim, flip, tilt on a ramp → Facing sprites
Collider shape, hurtbox, weak spot → Sprite hitbox
Clone, class with defaults, Svg, appearance, click → More Sprite features

Sprite constructor

Sprite(source, height=, width=, size=, center=, box=, frame=, offset=, hitbox_shape=, hitbox_source=, hitbox_anchor=, hitbox_scale=, flip_x=, flip_y=, art_angle=, angle=, visual=, shield_scale=, group=, layer=)

Name without =: 1st, in order: the file of a still image (PNG) or a Sheet. Name with =: by name. Catalog settings (cols= / atlas= / fps= / name= / yoyo=) belong on the Sheet — on the Sprite they are a TypeError.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
source1ststr or SheetA PNG (still image) or a Sheet. Lookup: Image files. E.g. Sprite("ship.png"). Several files: Sheet("a.png", "b.png"), then Sprite(sheet). A pattern with * is a TypeError (it means several frames): Sprite(Sheet("robot/Run (*).png", fps=12)).
height / width / sizename=numberPNG sizeDesign units, not pixels. size = the longer side. It measures the constructor frame (frame=; without it, the first frame of the first clip) and sets the Sprite's scale. With none of them, the Sheet's pixel_size applies (if it has one). See Different sizes.
centername=pointdesign center(x, y). It is the frame's pivot (with Sheet(anchor="bottom"), the feet).
boxname=Box or formulacellFits (keeping the PNG's aspect), or only centers if height= / width= / size= is given. Do not mix it with center=. With a formula (box=lambda: …), it follows the region: it grows through scale. box=.
framename=integer or str0The cell shown still: an index, or a name in the atlas. When the Sheet has a clip, an explicit frame= wins over autoplay.
offsetname=pair of numbers(0, 0)Shifts the drawing and the collider relative to center, in design units. It turns with the Sprite and mirrors with the flip. E.g. offset=(10, 0). Per clip, in art pixels: clip(offset=).
hitbox_shape / hitbox_source / hitbox_anchor / hitbox_scalename=str, number, tuple or pair"auto"The main hitbox: which shape, from which art, which point stays put, how much it shrinks. Later: sprite.hitbox.shape / .source / .anchor / .scale. See Sprite hitbox.
flip_x / flip_y / art_anglename=bool / numberFalse / 0Mirroring, and “which way the PNG points”. See Facing sprites.
anglename=numberrest_headingStarting heading in the world, in degrees. Omitted: the PNG appears as it was drawn. See Facing sprites.
visual / shield_scalename=Visual / numberNone / 1.4A Visual in the constructor. shield_scale is the size of the Shield around the silhouette. See Appearance and clicks.
group / layername=str—The same as in Every object on screen.
Sprite reference

Properties — image and size

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
frameinteger or str0read / writeCurrent cell. An index, or a name in the atlas. Writing a value stops the animation and shows that cell.
sheetSheetreadThis Sprite's catalog. Changes (clip / strip) are made on the Sheet, before you place the fleet — not through the shared catalog of Sprite("x.png").
width / height / sizenumber64read / writeSize of the current frame, in design units. play / frame= change what you read when the new frame has another size. Writing rescales every clip.
offsetpair(10, 0)read / writeShift of the drawing and the collider relative to center, in design units.
.boxBoxship.boxreadThe whole drawn cell (with the PNG's transparent margin), where it is drawn: pivot, offset, flip and scale all count. By the names: after a flip_x, box.top_center is still above the head. Higher on the screen: box.top. Measure.
.art_boxBoxship.art_boxreadOnly the frame's visible pixels on the screen (without the margin). It moves with the animation. Measure.
.is_collapsedboolFalsereadTrue if the drawn frame has no inside (w or h is zero, scale included). The constructor rejects a size ≤ 0; collapsing later is allowed and silent.

Properties — facing

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
flip_x / flip_yboolTrueread / writeMirrors the drawing and the collider. Rewrites .angle. Flip.
art_anglenumber90read / writeWhere the PNG's nose points, in degrees (0 = +x, 90 = +y), before the flip. Aim.
rest_headingnumber90readThe heading at which the PNG appears as drawn: art_angle after the flip. reset_rotation() comes back here.
tiltnumber · contact · "ground""ground"read / writeTilts only the drawing, around hitbox.anchor. It does not turn the body. Tilt.

Properties — collision

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
hitboxHitboxhero.hitboxreadThe main hitbox (stands, hits, resolve): .shape / .source / .anchor / .scale (writing them during the game works), .active, .box. Hitbox.
hitboxestuple of Hitboxhero.hitboxesreadAll of them: the main one first, then the extra ones from add_hitbox.

Properties — appearance

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.visualVisual or NoneHalo()read / writeMain Visual. None removes the Visual; add-ons stay.
.alphanumber0.5read / writeOpacity of the body, 0–1. It applies only to the image: Visuals that wrap the Sprite (Shield, Electric…) keep their own opacity.
.blendstr"add"read / writeHow the image mixes with what is already drawn. The same names as Shape. Default "normal". Blend.
.glow / .shadow / .hue / .gray / .tailbool or color or GlowTrueread / writeAdd-ons. .gray removes the color (0–1). See Add-ons.

Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
play(clip, loops=, next=, min_hold=, resume=)Parameters: clip (str), loops (number), next (str), min_hold (number), resume (True/False)selfPlays a clip from the Sheet. A visual, not a mode. Full table just below.
add_hitbox(group=, shape=, source=, anchor=, scale=, active=, px_rect=, px_circle=)Parameters: group (str or list), shape (str), source (default "each"), anchor, scale, active (True/False), px_rect (x, y, w, h), px_circle (x, y, r)HitboxAn extra hitbox, detection only. px_rect / px_circle: a shape by hand, instead of the four art parameters. Parts, Attack boxes.
showing(frames)Parameters: frames (clip name, index, frame name, or tuple / list)boolIs the frame on the screen one of these? It goes by the frame (right with yoyo, next=, an interrupted attack). Attack boxes.
remove_hitbox(part)Parameters: part (Hitbox)selfRemoves the extra hitbox. The Sprite leaves the groups that hitbox put it in; a group it was already in on its own stays. The main hitbox does not come off: sprite.hitbox.active = False.
reset_rotation()Optional: time, ease, then, on_done—Turns to rest_heading and sets tilt to zero. It does not clear the flip.
clone(center=, layer=, group=, frame=, scale=)Parameters: center (point), layer (str), group (str or list), frame (number), scale (number)the copied objectA new Sprite with this one's appearance. Clone.
set_alpha(alpha)Parameters: alpha (number 0–1)selfThe same as .alpha = alpha. It is not Shape.set_alpha (that one recolors fill/line).
look_like(other)Parameters: other (another object)—Copies the appearance of another object (color, Visual, add-ons).
save_visual() / restore_visual()No parameters—Remembers the current appearance (add-ons included) and goes back to it later (it keeps a single appearance). A second save_visual does nothing until restore_visual.
prepare_fx(Halo, Aura)Parameters: visuals (Visual)—Computes the silhouette of every frame ahead of time (avoids a hitch on the first Visual change). With no arguments: the current Visual, if it needs it.
play(clip, …)

sprite.play(clip, *, loops=, next=, min_hold=, resume=)

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
clip1ststrA name registered with sheet.clip / strip / fps= on the Sheet. E.g. sprite.play("walk") or sprite.play(clip="walk").
loops=name=integer or Noneloops=1 plays once and holds the last frame (or the first when yoyo=True), unless next= is given. Omitted: forever.
next=name=str or NoneThe clip that follows after loops. It is not then=. E.g. next="idle".
min_hold=name=number0Seconds. Until the current clip has played this long, requests for another clip are ignored.
resume=name=boolFalseWhen coming back to this clip, it continues from the remembered phase instead of restarting at frame 0. Leave it off for hit/hurt clips that must always start over.
Sheet

A Sheet holds the frames of one or more images and the animations (clips) made from them. It does not appear on the screen: hand it to a Sprite (Sprite(sheet)). One Sheet serves many Sprites.

Sheet(source, *files, cols=, rows=, cell=, atlas=, fps=, name=, yoyo=, anchor=, pixel_size=)

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
source1ststr, list or NoneA PNG, a file pattern ("robot/Run (*).png", Pattern) or a list of PNGs (2 Files), or left out with Sheet() (an option in 5 Strip). Atlas only: an XML/JSON on its own finds the PNG it lists. Lookup: Image files. E.g. Sheet("hero.png", cols=4, rows=3).
extra files2nd…strShortcut: Sheet("a.png", "b.png") = Sheet(["a.png", "b.png"]). A pattern here or in the list turns into its files, in its place. Incompatible with cols= / rows= / cell= / atlas= (use strip). A list in source= + extras: TypeError.
cols / rowsname=integer or NoneA regular grid. E.g. cols=4. Together: cols=4, rows=3. rows= without cols=: TypeError (a vertical strip is cols=1).
cellname=pair of numbers or NoneCell size in pixels. E.g. cell=(32, 32). Do not mix it with cols= / atlas=.
atlasname=str or NoneJSON/XML, with the PNG in source. E.g. atlas="sheet.json".
fpsname=number or NoneRegisters a clip over every cell already loaded. Without name=: "default". Grid and list. Packed atlas: TypeError.
namename=str or NoneThat clip's name. Needs fps=. In 5 Strip, name="idle" on the first file matches the strip calls that follow.
yoyoname=boolFalseBack and forth in the constructor's clip. Needs fps=.
anchorname=str or pair"center"The point of each PNG that sits on the Sprite's center: "center", "bottom", "top", "left", "right" or (ax, ay). A pivot written in the atlas wins. Different sizes.
pixel_sizename=number > 0 or NoneNoneThe size of one PNG pixel, in design units: pixel_size=3 → each pixel is worth 3 (pixel art at 3×); 0.5 → two pixels per unit (a large PNG). Sprites of this Sheet with no height= / width= / size= / box= draw at the PNG size × pixel_size — all at the same scale, without measuring each one. An explicit size on the Sprite wins. E.g. Sheet("tiles.png", cell=(16, 16), pixel_size=3).

Properties

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
nframesinteger8readHow many cells the catalog has now.
namestuple of strreadCell names (atlas / several files). A regular grid usually uses indices.
anchorstr or pair"center"readThe constructor's anchor=.
pixel_sizenumber or None3.0readThe constructor's pixel_size= (None if it was not given).

Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
clip(name, frames, fps=, yoyo=, offset=)Parameters: name (str), frames (list or omitted), fps (number, default 8), yoyo (bool), offset (pair of numbers)the SheetNames a sequence of cells already in the catalog (indices or atlas names). Without frames: every current cell. offset=(dx, dy): Different sizes. E.g. hero.clip("walk", [3, 4, 5, 6], fps=12).
strip(name, source, cols=, rows=, cell=, fps=, yoyo=, offset=)Parameters: name (str), source (str, pattern with * or list), cols / rows / cell, fps (number), yoyo (bool), offset (pair of numbers)the SheetAdds more frames and registers the clip (5 Strip). source: a strip file (a grid with cols=, or a single frame), a pattern ("ninja/Run__*.png": one file per frame, in order — File patterns) or a list of files. cols= / rows= / cell= with a pattern or a list: TypeError. Name first, like clip. Call it during setup, not every frame. E.g. hero.strip("walk", "walk.png", cols=8, fps=12), ninja.strip("running", "ninja/Run__*.png", fps=12).
frame_index(key)Parameters: key (number or str)integerResolves a cell index or name.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
Sprite("hero.png", cols=4, fps=8)a TypeError that points to the Sheet. cols= / rows= / cell= / atlas= / fps= / name= / yoyo= belong to the catalog.a shortcut on the Sprite
Sprite("x.png").sheet.clip(…)refused (TypeError). Sprite("x.png") shares one catalog among all the Sprites of that file. For clips, build a Sheet first.a copy made on demand
