Sprite · How to

Loading sprites

Six ways, depending on the files you have. In all of them, the Sheet builds the catalog and the Sprite places it.

You haveWay
One still PNG (potion, shot, ship)1 PNG — no Sheet
One PNG per frame (Run (1).png, Run (2).png…)2 Files
One packed PNG + XML/JSON, with animations3 Atlas
One PNG laid out as a regular grid4 Grid
One strip PNG per animation (idle.png, walk.png), or a pack of loose PNGs with several animations (Idle__000.png…, Run__000.png…)5 Strip
An atlas of items / ships; each Sprite stays on one frame6 Still image

One file, one still image. No Sheet, no clip, no play. The constructor already places the Sprite on the screen.

Sprite("potion.png", height=48, center=(x, y), group="potion")
Sprite(source="shot.png", height=18, center=(x, y))

Every Sprite("shot.png") shares one catalog (it decodes the file and computes the hitbox once). That is why this catalog refuses clip / strip. A Sheet("x.png") with no layout is a one-cell catalog of your own, and it takes clips.

Several files, each one a frame. A pattern with * takes them all at once; Sheet([...]) (or several positional arguments) lists them one by one; clip names sequences; play on the Sprite.

robot = Sheet("robot/Run (*).png", fps=12)   # Run (1).png, Run (2).png, … in order
Sprite(robot, height=56, center=(x, y))       # one clip → it starts playing

hero = Sheet(["Idle_0.png", "Idle_1.png", "Run_0.png", "Run_1.png"])
# the same: Sheet("Idle_0.png", "Idle_1.png", "Run_0.png", "Run_1.png")
hero.clip("idle", [0, 1], fps=6, yoyo=True)
hero.clip("run",  [2, 3], fps=12)
s = Sprite(hero, height=48, center=(x, y))
s.play("run")

"robot/Run (*).png" loads every file in that folder that matches, one per frame, in order. Rules: File patterns.

A pattern, a list or extra positional files = one file per frame. In this way, cols= / atlas= is a TypeError — that is 5 Strip. fps= in the constructor registers a clip over all the files. The frames also have names (the file's, without the extension): hero.clip("idle", ["Idle_0.png", "Idle_1.png"]).

PNGs of different sizes per animation (a lower slide, a wider fall) are common in trimmed packs. See Different sizes.

One PNG + a packed atlas (Kenney XML or JSON). Clips by frame name. The way taught here: image + atlas=.

space = Sheet("space_sheet.png", atlas="space_sheet.xml")
space.clip("green", ["enemyGreen1.png", "enemyGreen2.png"], fps=6)
enemy = Sprite(space, height=40, center=(x, y))
enemy.play("green")

A convenience: Sheet("space_sheet.xml") finds the PNG listed in the XML/JSON. Prefer naming both. If source= and the atlas list different PNGs, the author's source wins (a warning, once). If the source is missing, a warning, and it falls back to the listed PNG (or a placeholder). fps= / name= / yoyo= in the constructor of a packed atlas is a TypeError — it does not play every cell. The atlas can also carry pivots (Different sizes) and collision boxes (Atlas boxes).

One file laid out as a grid, cols= × rows= (or cell= in pixels). Several clips, or one loop with fps= on the Sheet.

run = Sheet("hero.png", cols=4, rows=3)
run.clip("walk", [3, 4, 5, 6], fps=12)
run.clip("jump", [7, 8, 9], fps=10)
Sprite(run, center=(200, 400)).play("walk")

snail = Sheet("snail.png", cols=8, fps=6)   # "default" clip over every cell
Sprite(snail, height=36, center=(x, y))    # one clip → it starts playing

Layout: cols= alone (one row), cols= with rows=, or cell=(w, h). The image must divide exactly. A vertical strip: cols=1, rows=8. cols= + cell= is a TypeError.

Each strip loads one animation and names its clip at once: a strip file, or a pattern with that animation's loose PNGs.

hero = Sheet("idle.png", cols=4, fps=6, name="idle")
hero.strip("walk", "walk.png", cols=8, fps=12)
hero.strip("jump", "jump.png", cols=4, fps=10)
# by name: hero.strip(name="walk", source="walk.png", cols=8, fps=12)
s = Sprite(hero, height=48, center=(x, y))
s.play("walk")

name= on the first file names the first clip. Strips are a grid or a single frame (a packed atlas stays in Sheet(..., atlas=)). A Sprite on a Sheet that is still empty is a ValueError.

A pack of loose PNGs (one file per frame, one prefix per animation): the Sheet starts empty and each strip gets a pattern. One line per animation, each name written once.

ninja = Sheet(anchor="bottom", pixel_size=0.16)
ninja.strip("idle", "ninja/Idle__*.png", fps=8)
ninja.strip("running", "ninja/Run__*.png", fps=12)
ninja.strip("jumping", "ninja/Jump__*.png", fps=10)
player = Sprite(ninja, center=(x, y))
player.play("running")

Rules for *: File patterns. "ninja/Jump__*.png" does not take Jump_Throw__000.png: the rest of the name must match letter by letter. A list works too: ninja.strip("flight", ["a.png", "b.png"], fps=8). With a pattern or a list, cols= / rows= / cell= is a TypeError (there is no image to cut).

One PNG + an atlas; each Sprite locks onto a named frame. No clip, no play.

space = Sheet("space_sheet.png", atlas="space_sheet.xml")
Sprite(space, frame="playerShip1_blue.png", height=48, center=(x, y))
Sprite(space, frame="powerup_bolt.png", height=24, center=(x2, y2))

frame= (an index or a name) picks the cell. Default 0. One Sheet for the whole fleet: the pixels and the atlas are read once.

Define the clips on the Sheet before (or while) you create the Sprites. A Sheet shared by a fleet is one and the same object: a new clip shows up for all of them.

File patterns: *

Art packs often come with one PNG per frame: Run__000.png, Run__001.png… Instead of listing them one by one, write the name with * where it changes. The * means “anything here”: Scena loads every file in that folder whose name matches, one frame per file, in order.

# Sheet: a single animation; fps= registers the clip.
# Run (1).png, Run (2).png, … Run (8).png
robot = Sheet("robot/Run (*).png", fps=12)
Sprite(robot, height=56, center=(200, 300))

# strip: one animation per line, the clip name first.
# "idle" = Idle__000.png … Idle__009.png
ninja = Sheet(anchor="bottom", pixel_size=0.16)
ninja.strip("idle", "ninja/Idle__*.png", fps=8)
ninja.strip("running", "ninja/Run__*.png", fps=12)
ninja.strip("jumping", "ninja/Jump__*.png", fps=10)
player = Sprite(ninja, center=(500, 300))
player.play("running")

# Among other files: the pattern turns into its files.
mix = Sheet("ninja/Idle__*.png", "ninja/Dead__009.png")
  1. Only * is special. It stands for any piece of the name (even none). The rest must match letter by letter: "ninja/Jump__*.png" does not take Jump_Throw__000.png. Case counts: "ninja/idle__*.png" does not find Idle__000.png.
  2. Natural order. Numbers in the name count as numbers: Run (2) comes before Run (10), with or without leading zeros (Run__002).
  3. One folder only. The * goes in the file name, not in the folder ("*/Run.png" is a ValueError). The lookup is the one in Image files, and the first folder that has a matching file wins — it never mixes folders.
  4. Nothing matched? The game goes on. A checkerboard in its place, and a warning with the pattern and the folders it looked in (and the names that differ only in case). The clip exists and plays.
  5. One file per frame. There is no single image to cut: cols= / rows= / cell= / atlas= with a pattern is a TypeError, even if only one file matches.

Where it works: wherever several files work — in Sheet (as source, in a list or among the extra files) and in strip. Sprite("ninja/Run__*.png") is a TypeError: a Sprite given a file name is a still image. Write Sprite(Sheet("ninja/Run__*.png", fps=12)). The frames get the file's name without the extension ("Run__003"), for use in clip, frame= and showing. Two files with the same name in different folders (idle/1.png and run/1.png) keep the name "1" from working for either of them (a ValueError naming both); use the path ("idle/1.png") or the index.

Without a pattern, the same thing as a list: ninja.strip("running", ["ninja/Run__000.png", "ninja/Run__001.png"], fps=12). Use it to pick only some frames or to change the order.

Sprite · How to

Animating sprites

The clip lives on the Sheet (which frames, fps, yoyo); the Sprite picks one with play. Animation is a visual, not a mode: it survives e.mode = ….

A named sequence on the Sheet; play on the Sprite. The same clip again, while it plays, does nothing — safe to call in update. A loops=1 clip that has already ended starts over: to play it only once from update, check first (if not player.showing("dead"):).

hero = Sheet("hero.png", cols=4, rows=3)
hero.clip("idle", [0, 1, 2], fps=6, yoyo=True)
hero.clip("walk", [3, 4, 5, 6], fps=12)
sprite = Sprite(hero, center=(200, 400))   # 2+ clips → still on the first frame of "idle"
sprite.play("walk")
sprite.play("walk")                        # does nothing: the animation goes on
sprite.frame = 3                           # stops playback and shows cell 3
The Sheet hasSprite(sheet) starts
0 clipsStill on frame (default 0).
1 clipPlaying that clip (autoplay).
2+ clipsStill on the first frame of the first registered clip, until .play.
An explicit frame=Still on that cell — it wins over autoplay.

yoyo=True goes back and forth; yoyo=False starts over from the beginning. fps omitted in clip = 8. The time is the world's × the Sprite's time_scale: it pauses with the world, and sprite.time_scale = 0.5 animates in slow motion.

Which frame am I on? sprite.showing("walk"), showing(3) or showing((3, 7)) say whether the frame on the screen is one of these — for example, dust on the footstep frames: if player.showing((3, 7)): drop_dust(). To switch on an attack box on certain frames: Attack boxes.

A short reaction: it plays once and goes back to the base clip.

hero = Sheet("hero.png", cols=4, rows=3)
hero.clip("idle", [0, 1, 2], fps=6, yoyo=True)
hero.clip("hit", [9, 10], fps=12)
hero.clip("die", [11], fps=8)
sprite = Sprite(hero, center=(200, 400))
sprite.play("hit", loops=1, next="idle")   # once, then "idle"
sprite.play("die", loops=1)                # once, and hold the last frame

loops=1 without next= holds the last frame (the first, in a yoyo clip). next= is a clip name, not a callback — to run code at the end, use after.

Pick the clip every frame from the state. min_hold and resume keep it from flickering and restarting.

# grounded can flicker for one frame — min_hold keeps the clip from restarting;
# resume=True continues the phase on the way back (leave it off for one-shot reactions).
if not grounded:
    sprite.play("jump", min_hold=0.06)
elif sprite.vel.x != 0:
    sprite.play("walk", min_hold=0.08, resume=True)
else:
    sprite.play("idle", min_hold=0.08, resume=True)

Off by default: without min_hold / resume, each switch takes effect at once and starts over from frame 0. To turn the hero toward the way it runs: Flip.

Packs trimmed per animation have PNGs of different sizes. One scale per Sprite and a shared registration point solve it without editing the art.

ninja = Sheet(anchor="bottom")
ninja.strip("idle", "ninja/Idle__*.png", fps=8)
ninja.strip("sliding", "ninja/Slide__*.png", fps=12)
player = Sprite(ninja, height=70, center=(x, y))   # center = the feet
player.play("sliding")                            # ~56 tall, on the ground

# or: the scale on the art, once — no height= on each Sprite
tiles = Sheet("tiles.png", cell=(16, 16), pixel_size=3)
ground_tile = Sprite(tiles, center=(x, y))        # 16 px cell × 3 = 48
RuleWhat it does
Sheet(pixel_size=)The art's scale, once on the Sheet: the size of one PNG pixel in design units (3 = pixel art at 3×; 0.5 = two pixels per unit). Sprites of the Sheet with no size in the constructor draw at the PNG size × pixel_size: a 16 px tile and a 32 px hero stay 1:2, without measuring each Sprite. A size on the Sprite wins (for that Sprite). A standalone PNG: Sprite(Sheet("tree.png", pixel_size=3)).
One scale per Spriteheight= / width= / size= measure the constructor frame (frame=; without it, the first frame of the first clip). The other frames draw at their PNG size × that scale: a 351 px slide next to a 439 px idle, with height=70, ends up 56 tall. sprite.height reads the current frame. Writing the size rescales every clip.
Sheet(anchor=)Which point of each PNG sits on center. "bottom": the bottom center of every frame sits at the feet, and a shorter frame stays on the ground. Values: "center" (default), "bottom", "top", "left", "right" or (ax, ay), y up.
Atlas pivotA pivot written in the atlas (pivot / anchor / origin in JSON, pivotX / pivotY in XML) wins over anchor=.
clip(…, offset=(dx, dy))The fine adjustment when one clip does not line up with the others: it moves that clip's art in art pixels (y up, +x = right in the unflipped art). It mirrors with flip_x. Also in strip(…, offset=). A cell has only one offset: the same cell in two clips with different offsets is a ValueError.
Sprite(offset=)Another adjustment: it shifts the whole Sprite (drawing and collider) in design units, in every clip.

The collision body measures its own reference frame, not the frame that is playing: the hero does not grow or shrink when it switches clips. See Body.

Sprite · How to

Facing sprites

Three different questions: where the PNG points (art_angle), where the Sprite points in the world (.angle) and how much the drawing tilts without moving the collider (tilt). flip_x / flip_y mirror it.

art_angle says where the nose is drawn in the PNG. With it, .angle becomes the heading in the world — the same number as heading().

# The ship is drawn pointing up (+y).
ship = Sprite("ship.png", height=48, art_angle=90)
ship.angle                          # 90: it appears as drawn

ship.rotate_to(heading(ship, mouse))   # the nose points at the mouse
bullet.move_to(goal, time=1.2, face=True)
ship.reset_rotation()                  # back to rest_heading (90)
FieldMeaning
art_angleDegrees, the same convention as the world (0 = +x, 90 = +y): the nose of the pixels, before the flip. One value per Sprite, for every frame. Default 0 (art facing right). Writing it later does not rewrite .angle.
.angleHeading in the world: where the painted front points. The constructor starts at rest_heading, so the PNG appears as drawn.
rest_headingRead-only. The heading at which the PNG appears with no rotation: art_angle after the flip. A ship with art_angle=90 → 90; a ninja with art_angle=0 + flip_x → 180. Shape: 0.
reset_rotation()Turns to rest_heading and sets tilt to zero. It does not clear the flip. It takes time= / ease= like the other moves.

It mirrors around the pivot, before the rotation. The collider and the parts mirror along with it, without being recomputed.

# The ninja is drawn facing right.
if keyp("LEFT"):
    hero.flip_x = True     # faces left; angle becomes 180
elif keyp("RIGHT"):
    hero.flip_x = False    # angle goes back to 0

Turning on a flip rewrites .angle (flip_x → 180 − θ, flip_y → −θ) so that .angle is still the way the painted front points. Writing the same value again does nothing. clip(offset=), Sprite(offset=), hitbox_anchor and the tilt pivot mirror along with it. Do not use a negative scale to mirror — drawing uses the absolute value.

tilt tilts only the drawing — on a ramp, for example. The body stays upright, and center stays where resolve put it.

collision.floor = True      # "ground" belongs to a world with a floor
hero = Sprite(ninja, hitbox_shape="rect", hitbox_anchor="bottom")

def update(dt):
    hero.tilt = "ground"   # or AUTO_GROUND: follows the ground; in the air it goes back to 0

# Other ways:
hero.tilt = 22             # just that angle
hero.tilt = 0              # off
ValueEffect
numberTurns the drawing by that angle. It does not shift it.
"ground" / AUTO_GROUNDReads, every frame, the slope_angle of a "bottom" contact (touching). In the air: 0. It belongs to a world with a floor (collision.floor = True); with no floor, it warns once.
a contact cUses c.slope_angle and stays until you overwrite it. In update, reset it to zero before the loop over the contacts.

The pivot is the hitbox_anchor of the computed collider (not the PNG's rectangle). With a "bottom" anchor and a "bottom" contact, "ground" and tilt = c also bring the drawing down onto the ramp's plane, only along the normal (they do not slide sideways). With "center", the drawing does not come down to the ramp. Parts follow the tilt; the body does not. reset_rotation() sets it to zero.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
On a ramp, hero.angle = rest_heading + slopeturning the collider too, and the hero stumbles. Use tilt: only the drawing.tilt
ship.rotate_to(heading(ship, goal) + art_angle)adding art_angle twice. .angle is already the heading in the world: ship.rotate_to(heading(ship, goal)).a manual adjustment
A “rotated” frame in a packed atlaspart of how the atlas is packed, resolved when it is read. It has nothing to do with art_angle.art_angle

Sprite · How to

Sprite hitbox

The shape a Sprite collides with. Every hitbox is a Hitbox: the main one (sprite.hitbox) for floor, walls and resolve; extra ones (add_hitbox) that only detect — a hurtbox, a weak spot. Both have the same properties: shape · source · anchor · scale · active · box.

Main (sprite.hitbox)Extra (add_hitbox)
Created byThe constructor: Sprite(hitbox_shape=…, hitbox_scale=…)sprite.add_hitbox(group=…, scale=…)
How manyOne (every Graphic has it; on a Shape it is the geometry itself)Several
Used forresolve (standing, bumping), a @collide that names the SpriteDetection only, through the groups it claims
GroupsThe Sprite's (sprite.tag(…))The ones it claims (group=)
Default sourceThe constructor's frame: steady while it animates"each": follows the current frame
Switch off only this onesprite.hitbox.active = False (the extras keep going)extra.active = False
Measuresprite.hitbox.boxextra.box
Follows tiltNo (stays upright)Yes
Frame with no artFalls back to the drawing's boxNo collider on that frame
Shape by hand—px_rect= / px_circle=, in the frame's pixels (Attack boxes)
Switched on by frame—part["active"] @= lambda: sprite.showing(…)

Both take the same four parameters. In the Sprite constructor they carry the hitbox_ prefix (the Sprite has its own scale); on the hitbox they don't: Sprite(hitbox_scale=0.8) is sprite.hitbox.scale = 0.8, and on an extra it is add_hitbox(scale=0.8) / extra.scale = 0.8.

ParameterQuestionValuesDefault
hitbox_shape= · .shapeWhich shape?"auto" · "rect" · "ellipse" · "circle" · "hull""auto"
hitbox_source= · .sourceFrom which art?frame · clip · tuple of clips · "all" · "clip" · "each"the constructor's frame (part: "each")
hitbox_anchor= · .anchorWhich point stays put?"center" · "bottom" · "top" · "left" · "right" · (ax, ay)"center"
hitbox_scale= · .scaleHow much to shrink / stretch?number or (sx, sy)(1.0, 1.0)

When it is computed. The first time the Sprite enters collision (@collide, resolve, collidable = True). A purely decorative Sprite never pays. The result is cached per image: a hundred Sprite("shot.png") share a single computation. After that the main hitbox stays frozen while the clip plays — except with "each" (every frame) and "clip" (on every clip change). See it: collision.show_colliders() or Ctrl+Shift+7 — main hitboxes in a resolve in gold, other main hitboxes in green, extras in cyan.

Measure the Sprite

ReadMeasuresWhich frame
sprite.width / heightThe size you gave (the setting; writing rescales).fixed
sprite.boxThe whole drawn cell, transparent margin included, where it is drawn.the one on screen
sprite.hitbox.boxThe main hitbox, as collision uses it. This is the one for floor_below(dx=).the source's (default: fixed)
extra.boxThat extra hitbox (None on a frame with no collider).the source's (default: the one on screen)
sprite.art_boxOnly the visible pixels of the frame on screen.the one on screen

Each read is a new Box, as things are right now: hit_width = hero.hitbox.box.width. Hitbox boxes are aligned to the screen (left / right / bottom / top); box and art_box turn with the Sprite. Measuring does not sign anything up for collision.

The main hitbox. Pick the shape with hitbox_shape= and the art that defines it with hitbox_source= (later: sprite.hitbox.shape / .source).

Sprite("ship.png")                          # "auto": picks the shape on its own
Sprite("ball.png", hitbox_shape="circle")
Sprite("swordsman.png", hitbox_shape="hull")

hero_sheet = Sheet("hero.png", cols=4, rows=3)
hero_sheet.clip("idle", [0, 1], fps=6)
hero_sheet.clip("running", [2, 3, 4, 5], fps=12)
hero_sheet.clip("dead", [9, 10, 11], fps=8)
hero = Sprite(hero_sheet, hitbox_shape="rect", hitbox_source=("idle", "running"))

shape — which shape

ValueFitWhen to use
"auto"Tries a circle, circles, an ellipse, two ellipses, a convex hull and a rectangle, and keeps the best fit for the lowest cost. It prefers to err on the inside: a phantom touch is worse than a missed one.Ships, enemies, loose objects.
"rect"The silhouette's box: covers all the art, flat base.Anything that walks — platformers.
"ellipse"An ellipse in the silhouette's box. Nearly square becomes a circle.Oval bodies.
"circle"A circle that covers the art.Balls, coins.
"hull"The silhouette's convex hull (a little bigger than the art).Pointy shapes.

Naming a shape means covering the art with it. Only "auto" chooses by precision.

source — from which art

One rule: one frame is that frame; several frames are their union (the silhouettes are overlaid at the pivot and fitted once — not a union of shapes).

ValueWhich artComputed
omittedThe constructor's frame (frame=; without it, the first frame of the first clip).once
3 / "Idle__004"That frame (index or name in the atlas).once
"running"Union of that clip's frames.once
("idle", "running")Union of those clips, and only those. An empty tuple or an unknown name: ValueError.once
"all"Union of every registered clip. With no clips (a fleet of still images): the constructor's frame. Not the whole atlas.once
"clip"Union of the clip that is playing. Nothing playing: the constructor's frame.on every clip change
"each"The current frame.every frame

The tuple is the right choice when one clip is very different from the others: above, the wide frames of "dead" do not widen the hitbox of a walking hero. With "auto" + "each" / "clip", the kind of shape is chosen the first time; after that only the size changes. The main hitbox measures its reference frames, not the frame that is playing: the hero does not grow when a taller clip plays.

"each" and "clip" move the foot line on every frame / clip. For anything that walks on the floor, use a fixed set ("all", one clip or a tuple).

The computed shape covers the silhouette. scale shrinks or stretches it around anchor (in the constructor: hitbox_scale= / hitbox_anchor=).

# Platformer recipe: a steady box, feet on the floor, narrower than the art.
hero = Sprite(
    hero_sheet,
    hitbox_shape="rect",
    hitbox_source="all",
    hitbox_anchor="bottom",
    hitbox_scale=(0.55, 1.0),
)

Sprite("swordsman.png", hitbox_shape="hull", hitbox_anchor=(-0.5, 0))
AnchorPairCollider point
"center"(0, 0)center (moves nothing)
"bottom"(0, -1)middle of the base
"top"(0, 1)middle of the top
"left"(-1, 0)middle of the left side
"right"(1, 0)middle of the right side
—(-0.5, 0.2)left of center, a little above

The anchor does three things:

  1. It fixes the scale. (0.55, 1.0) + "bottom" narrows without lifting the feet.
  2. It pins the shape to the art. The anchor point lines up with the silhouette box of the frames in this computation (source) — not with the whole Sheet. A circle or ellipse with "bottom" rests its base on the foot line.
  3. It is the pivot for tilt. With a flip, the point mirrors along with the collider.

The pair is not limited to −1…1 (it can go past the edge). Written as a name, it reads back as a name; as a pair, it reads back as a pair. scale: one number applies to both axes; it always reads back as (sx, sy); 0 flattens that axis; a negative number, nan or inf is a ValueError. The PNG's transparent margin stays in the file — height= still measures that canvas; it is the hitbox computation that finds the silhouette.

A single main hitbox gives stability. When the pose really changes (the hero goes into the water and swims horizontally), switch it by hand: all four parameters can be written during the game.

STANDING = ("idle", "running", "jumping")

hero = Sprite(ninja, group="hero", hitbox_shape="rect", hitbox_source=STANDING,
               hitbox_anchor="bottom", hitbox_scale=(0.55, 1.0))

def enter_water():
    hero.hitbox.source = ("swimming", "floating")   # union of the two clips
    hero.hitbox.anchor = "center"
    hero.hitbox.scale = (1.0, 0.55)             # horizontal pose: flattens the height
    hero.play("swimming")

def leave_water():
    hero.hitbox.source = STANDING
    hero.hitbox.anchor = "bottom"
    hero.hitbox.scale = (0.55, 1.0)
    hero.play("idle")

It is still the same Sprite: groups, collision functions and resolve do not change. Writing shape or source computes it again (cached after the first time); anchor and scale only reposition. You can also change the shape: hero.hitbox.shape = "ellipse".

TopicRule
By hand × "clip"hitbox_source="clip" switches on its own, but for every clip: the foot line follows each one. It suits things that fly or a top-down view. For anything that walks, switch by hand only at the moments that call for it.
The hitbox grows into a wallIf the new shape cuts into a solid that was clear, resolve pushes it back out through that face. See resolve.
Wrong nameChecked on write: an unknown clip or frame is a ValueError. If the Sheet loses the clip later, the computation uses the constructor's frame and warns once.

An extra hitbox that owns a group and only detects. The main hitbox still takes care of floor and walls.

hero = Sprite(ninja, group="hero", hitbox_shape="rect", hitbox_source="all",
               hitbox_anchor="bottom", hitbox_scale=(0.55, 1.0))
hurt = hero.add_hitbox(group="hurt")      # silhouette of the current frame; only detects

resolve(hero, "ground")                    # the main hitbox stands on the ground

@collide("bullet", "hurt")                   # the part answers for "hurt"
def wounded(bullet, victim, info):             # victim is hero; info.b_hitbox is hurt
    victim.hp -= 1
    bullet.destroy()

What group="hurt" does. Two things: the Sprite joins the "hurt" group (like any tag: group["hurt"] lists the Sprite, hero.tagged("hurt") is True), and the part claims the group — in collision, under "hurt", the one that shows up is the extra, not the main hitbox. A part can claim several groups (group=["hurt", "mark"]). Two colliders of the same Sprite do not answer for the same group: a second part with "hurt" raises an error.

What answers

You writeWhat collides
@collide(bullet, hero) · ANYTHING · on_collideThe main hitbox. Naming the Sprite means the main hitbox (@collide(bullet, hero.hitbox) raises an error: name the Sprite).
@collide("bullet", "hurt")The part that claims "hurt".
@collide("bullet", hurt)The part (the Hitbox object).
Collision functionAlways receives the Sprite. info.a_hitbox / info.b_hitbox say which part (None = the main one). CollisionInfo.
resolve(hurt, …)TypeError: a part does not resolve.
resolve("enemy", …) with parts in "enemy"Moves the Sprites by their main hitbox. A boss with a weak spot and wasps in the same group still stand.
info.push_apart() / bounce_apart() / resolve() on a part's contactRaises an error. normal, point and depth can still be read.
touching_sides / touching_contactsOnly the main hitbox. Extras never count.

A Sprite never collides with its own parts, and two parts of the same Sprite never form a pair.

Switching on and off

I wantWriteEffect
Invincible for a whilehero.untag("hurt") … hero.tag("hurt")The Sprite leaves the group; the part still owns "hurt" and comes back with the tag.
Switch off only the extrahurt.active = FalseLeaves play (fires the exits). True switches it back on.
Switch off only the main onehero.hitbox.active = FalseGoes through floor and walls (a ghost); the extras keep detecting. True switches it back on. Everything: collidable = False.
Give up the claimhurt.remove_from_group("hurt")The part drops the group and the Sprite leaves it.
Remove the parthero.remove_hitbox(hurt)The Sprite leaves the groups the part put it in. A boss with group="enemy" stays in "enemy" when its weak spot add_hitbox(group=["enemy", "weak"]) is removed.

The group counts for detection and resolution. If "enemy" is a side of a resolve, untag("enemy") also takes the Sprite off the floor. For invincibility, toggle a group that is not a side of a resolve (such as "hurt").

Lifetime

  • Dies with the Sprite: destroy() fires the exits and kills the parts (is_alive False, host None).
  • hero.active = False and collidable = False switch off every hitbox; turning them back on switches them back on.
  • A frame with no art (with "each") = the part is absent on that frame. @collide / @collide_exit fire when it appears / disappears.
  • Follows the drawing: pose, flip, scale, offset, current frame and tilt.
  • clone() does not copy parts. Create them in the class's setup():
class Hero(Sprite):
    def setup(self):
        self.hurt = self.add_hitbox(group="hurt")

Queries and cost

A query with no group (query_point, query_circle, raycast(group=None), collides_with()) sees only the main hitboxes. With the group, it sees the parts: collision.raycast(tower, p2=hero, group="hurt"), collides_with("hurt"). A query never hits the parts of whoever is asking. See Queries.

Each part costs ~11–12 µs per step on this development machine: 20 animated Sprites with one part add up to ~0.26 ms; 100, ~1.2 ms. Fine for a hero, a boss and a squad. A fleet of 100 that needs only one collider keeps just the main hitbox.

A JSON / XML atlas can carry collision boxes per frame (hitboxes). Every "auto" computation of the Sprite uses them instead of the silhouette.

fighter = Sheet("fighter.png", atlas="fighter.json")   # frames with "hitboxes"

# A main hitbox with an explicit shape ignores the boxes: it keeps the silhouette.
p1 = Sprite(fighter, hitbox_shape="rect", hitbox_source="all", hitbox_anchor="bottom")

# An "auto" + "each" extra reads the current frame's boxes.
strike_boxes = p1.add_hitbox(group="strike")
  • They apply to every "auto" computation — the main hitbox included, because "auto" is the default. An explicit shape ("rect", "ellipse", "circle", "hull") ignores them.
  • Today, in practice, it is one set of boxes per Sprite: give the main hitbox an explicit shape and let an "auto" extra read the boxes.
  • With "each", each frame uses its own boxes. A computation over several frames at once (clip, tuple, "all") uses the boxes of the set's first frame.
  • hitbox_anchor="bottom" rests on the written boxes, not on the silhouette.

The area that hits (the sword, the punch): a part with its shape set by hand, which switches on by itself on the frames of the strike.

hero_sheet.clip("strike", [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15], fps=14)
STRIKE = (12, 13, 14)                              # frames with the sword stretched out

sword = hero.add_hitbox(group="attack", px_rect=(430, 180, 90, 80))
sword["active"] @= lambda: hero.showing(STRIKE)

def attack():
    hero.play("strike", loops=1, next="idle")   # the box switches on and off by itself

@collide("attack", "enemy")
def landed(hero, enemy, info):
    enemy.destroy()

Shape by hand: px_rect and px_circle

ParameterNumbers
px_rect=(x, y, w, h)Top-left corner and size, in the frame's pixels.
px_circle=(x, y, r)Center and radius, in the frame's pixels.

The numbers are the ones your image editor shows for that frame: origin at the top-left corner, y pointing down. It is an address in the image; the rest of Scena keeps y pointing up. The box stays attached to the drawing: Sheet(anchor=), clip(offset=), offset, flip, rotation, scale and tilt carry it along — you never add offsets yourself. It can go past the edge of the frame.

  • One PNG per frame, or one frame in Aseprite: the number the editor shows.
  • A grid sheet (cols=) opened as a single image: subtract the cell's origin (column × cell width, row × cell height).
  • A packed atlas: pixels of the original, untrimmed frame; Scena undoes the trimming and the rotation.
  • The same numbers on a frame of another size land somewhere else. Switch the part on only on the frames you measured.
  • One shape per part, and it does not mix with shape= / source= / anchor= / scale= (TypeError). sword.px_rect = None goes back to the art.
  • Only on a sheet Sprite: on an Svg it is a TypeError.

Switching on by frame: showing and @=

hero.showing(frames) says whether the frame on screen is one of these: a clip name, an index, a frame name, or a tuple / list mixing them. It goes by frame, so it stays right through yoyo, resume=, next= and an interrupted strike.

sword["active"] @= lambda: … links the switch to a formula. Scena computes it at the start of each frame's collision step — after update, on_update and any play() — and on every read of sword.active. The formula can read anything (hero.showing(…)), even values that are not Scena fields — as in group[...] @=.

I wantWriteEffect
The box only on the strike's framessword["active"] @= lambda: hero.showing(STRIKE)Comes in on the strike's first frame, leaves after the last.
Let go of the formulasword["active"].unlink()The last value stays; .active = … works again.
Invincible for 1.5 shurt.active = False and after(1.5, rearm)Time decides, not the drawing: a plain write.
Write while the formula is linkedsword.active = TrueLinkedAttributeError: let go first with unlink().

Why not @when? It runs after collision: the box switches on and off one frame late (one game loop). A line in update (sword.active = hero.showing(STRIKE)) works, but it lags if a play() comes after it in the same game frame, and it stays on if the hero changes mode in the middle of the strike and nobody writes the line again.

The formula only reads: do not move things or change groups inside it. If it raises an error, the message points to the @= line and to the add_hitbox line. Boxes written in the atlas: Atlas boxes.

Hitbox

Every hitbox. The main one is g.hitbox on any Graphic (on a Shape, the geometry itself: shape is read-only, the other three raise TypeError; Text has none). Extras: sprite.add_hitbox(…) — calling Hitbox(…) directly raises TypeError. It is not an Entity: no pose, no drawing, no own fields. Extras on Sprite and Svg (px_rect / px_circle only on a sheet Sprite).

After remove_hitbox or the owner's destroy(), reads still work (hb.shape, hb.scale; hb.box is None) and every write raises DestroyedError saying where it was destroyed — guard with if hb.is_alive:. Read-only fields (box, host, is_alive, layer, group) say what to write instead.

Properties

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
shape / source / anchor / scalestr, pair or tuple"each"read / writeThe four parameters. On an extra, source defaults to "each".
.boxBox or Nonehero.hitbox.box.widthreadThis hitbox as it is now, aligned to the screen. None on a frame with no collider. Measures even when switched off. Measure.
px_rect / px_circletuple or None(430, 180, 90, 80)read / writeExtras only. A shape by hand in the frame's pixels (y down). Writing one clears the other; None goes back to the art. Attack boxes.
.activeboolTrueread / writeSwitches only this hitbox on / off (on the main one, the extras keep going; collidable switches them all off). It can be linked to a formula (below); then writing raises LinkedAttributeError.
.groupfrozenset{"hurt"}readExtra: the groups it claims. Main: the Sprite's groups minus the ones an extra claims (the extra answers for those). Read-only: change it with hb.tag / untag (main: sprite.tag).
.hostSprite or NonereadThe owner. None once removed or once the owner is destroyed.
.is_aliveboolTruereadTrue until remove_hitbox or the owner's destroy().

Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
add_to_group(groupid) / remove_from_group(groupid)Parameters: groupid (str)the partExtras only. Claims / drops a group. Dropping also takes the Sprite out of the group. On the main hitbox, tagged(name) answers (it is name in hitbox.group); the others raise TypeError.
tag(*names) / untag(*names) / tagged(name)Parameters: names (names); tagged takes name (a name)the part / boolThe same thing, in the tag vocabulary.
part["active"] @= fn / part["active"].unlink()Parameters: fn (function with no arguments that returns True / False)—Links the switch to a formula (main or extra), computed in each frame's collision step. unlink() lets go and keeps the last value. Only "active" can be linked.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
sprite.box.width as the hitbox widthsprite.hitbox.box.width. The drawing's box includes the PNG's transparent margin.the collider
sprite.hitbox.active = False = collidable = FalseSwitches off only the main hitbox; the extras keep going. collidable = False switches them all off.switching off the Sprite
Track(sprite) as a hurtboxTrack(sprite) is the live outline (for building, drawing). A hurtbox is add_hitbox.a damage collider
A click hits the hitbox@click / contains_point look at the current frame's alpha. collision.query_point looks at the bodies.the hitbox
hitbox_source="all" = the whole SheetThe union of the registered clips. An atlas with lasers and ships does not go in whole.every cell
px_rect with y pointing upThe frame's pixels as the editor shows them: y pointing down, origin at the top-left corner. The rest of Scena has y pointing up.a world coordinate
showing("strike") = the strike clip is playingThe strike clip's frames are on screen. A frame two clips share counts for both.the current clip's name
@when to switch on the strike boxpart["active"] @= lambda: … is computed before the collision of the same game frame. @when runs after: one frame late.the way to switch on the box
The Shield follows the hitboxThe Shield uses the frames' silhouette (× shield_scale). The hitbox parameters do not change it.the collider

Sprite

More Sprite features

Past the basics: copying a Sprite, giving a class defaults, using SVG as a sprite, appearance and clicks.

A new Sprite that looks like this one. Useful for building a fleet from a template. It is not a pool.

class Ship(Sprite, source="playerShip1_blue.png", height=48, group="ship"):
    pass

_SHIP = Ship(layer=None)    # template: off screen
_SHIP.active = False        # neither runs nor collides
ship_a = _SHIP.clone(center=(120, 400))
ship_b = _SHIP.clone(center=(240, 400))
ship_c = _SHIP.clone(center=(360, 400))
Copied (a snapshot of now)Fresh
Sheet, frame, size, offset, hitbox parameters, art_anglesetup() always runs
Pose: angle, scale, flip, tilt (the clone points where the original points; clone(scale=) multiplies)
Visual and add-ons (look_like)Own fields, mode, timers, click callbacks
Groups (tags included), unless group=Hitbox parts (create them in setup())
visibleAnimation position

layer= is placement: omitted, it uses the class default; layer=None stays off screen (a template). group= replaces the groups entirely. Clone a clean template, not a hero that is already tagged ("shielded" would come along). To shoot, build a new one: Shot(center=…) costs the same as clone().

Shapes, Text and Track follow the same rule: the clone matches the original, with the same pose and the same points (a Rect's p1 is still its p1), and center= puts it somewhere else (_ROCK.clone(center=(300, 50))). frame= exists only on Sprite: on the others it raises TypeError. A Text pinned by top_left= makes a clone pinned by the same corner.

Appearance defaults go on the class line. Each instance only says where it goes.

space = Sheet("space_sheet.png", atlas="space_sheet.xml")

class Shot(Sprite, source=space, frame="laserBlue01.png", height=18,
           art_angle=90, group="shot"):
    def setup(self):
        self.damage = 1

Shot(center=ship.center)
Shot(center=ship.center, frame="laserRed01.png")   # the instance wins

These work on the class line: source, frame, height / width / size, the four hitbox parameters, offset, visual, shield_scale, group, flip_x / flip_y, art_angle. A subclass inherits and overrides them. Placement (center, layer, box) is refused on the class. Do not write frame = … or height = … as an attribute in the class body: Scena does not read the value from there, and the class definition raises TypeError with the fix. Pass it on the class line.

Svg is a Sprite whose body comes from an SVG: <svg …> markup or a file. A still image: no clips, no play.

compass = Svg("compass.svg", height=48, center=(x, y))
Svg("<svg …>", height=48)
compass.svg = lib.render()   # reloads (markup or file)

Svg(source, height=, width=, size=, center=, box=, hitbox_shape=, hitbox_source=, hitbox_anchor=, hitbox_scale=, group=, layer=)

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
source1ststr<svg …> text or a file name. Without < it is a file. Search: Image files. E.g. Svg("compass.svg").
height / width / sizename=number or NoneDesign units. E.g. height=48.
centername=pointdesign center(x, y).
boxname=Box or formulacellSame as Sprite. With a formula (box=lambda: …), it follows the region: grows through scale. box=.
hitboxname=—The same parameters as Sprite; "all" / "each" / "clip" come out the same (one frame). add_hitbox works too.
PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.svgstr"<svg …>"read / writeThe current markup — the text, never the path. Assigning reloads it (markup or file). The same string does nothing. On failure: a warning, and the last good body stays. None clears it: back to the checkerboard, like Svg(None).
.boxBoxicon.boxreadA copy of the visual frame, taken now, with the names: after a flip_x, box.top_center is still over the head. Higher on screen: box.top. Place.

It becomes a bitmap when it loads: camera zoom smooths it, it does not redraw the vector. cols= / atlas= / fps=, play and strip are a TypeError. clone() copies the markup.

The visuals and add-ons from Appearance work on Sprite. A few details are Sprite's own.

sprite.alpha = 0.5
sprite.blend = "add"
sprite.glow = True
sprite.visual = Halo()
sprite.shield_scale = 1.6            # Shield oval bigger than the silhouette

# Loading screen: warm up before switching visuals during play.
sprite.prepare_fx(Halo, Aura)
  • alpha and blend apply to the image.
  • Silhouette visuals (Halo, Aura, Rim, Laser…) compute the current clip's silhouette when you assign .visual. prepare_fx(*visuals) computes every frame in advance; with no arguments, the current visual. Which visuals a Sprite takes: Visual.
  • Shield wraps the union of the frames' silhouettes, times shield_scale (default 1.4). Changing clips does not make the shell jump.
  • look_like(other) copies the visual and add-ons; save_visual() / restore_visual() store them and bring them back.
  • Clicks: @click and contains_point look at the current frame's alpha (tilt included). A transparent pixel does not click. It is not the hitbox.

Track

A curve. It serves two purposes: a track for move_along and a stroke you can draw (a curved wall, a ring that fills up). Default: invisible, like Point. Any Shape is also a track: bug.move_along(hexagon, time=4).

orbit = Track.circle(center=lambda: earth.center, radius=120)
moon.move_along(orbit, time=4, loops="forever")
wasp.move_along(Track.eight(width=90, height=40), time=2.5)
track = Track(points=[(80, 200), (240, 380), (520, 160)], color="gold")
t1 = Track(sprite1)

Anchored or floating. This is the choice that changes how a track behaves:

AnchoredFloating
Where it isAt a place in the world. The traveler goes to it.No place of its own for the trip: the curve starts where the traveler is (or at the point at= of move_along).
WhenYou passed a placement word: center=, points=, p1=, start=, or a Shape (Track(hexagon)).Sizes only: Track.eight(width=90), Track.circle(radius=80), vectors= without start=, Track(), a preset name ("eight").
Typical useAn orbit around a planet, a curved wall, a fixed path in the level.“Do a figure eight from where you are”: patrol, dodge, dance.

An explicit floating= always wins. Every Track has a real .center — floating is not “no position”; .is_floating only says whether the track's pose holds the traveler.

Giving it a place later anchors it. A track that floats only because it was made without a placement anchors when you give it a place later: linking the center (orbit["center"] @= lambda: earth.center), writing .center = or moving it (move_to, move_by). That is the missing placement, the same as center= in the constructor; anything already traveling on it starts following it. Rotating or scaling is not placement. With floating=True (or is_floating = True) it keeps floating: moving it only changes where it is drawn.

Visible or not. A motion-only track (no color= / visual= / line_width= / visible=True / layer=) stays out of the draw list — you can travel on it, and it goes away when nothing holds on to it. With a style, visible=True or an explicit layer=, it enters the canvas as a Shape (stroke, clicks and collision); hidden with visible = False, it stays there (it just does not show): an invisible collision strip — the track of a race, queried with collision.query_point — does not go away. To see tracks during development: show_tracks(True) (magenta; it does not turn on visible) — see Debug.

Four ways to give the shape: positions (points=), relative steps (vectors=), the outline of a Shape, or a preset.

Track()                                          # Track.eight(); floats
Track(points=[(60, 80), (200, 300), (420, 120)]) # curve (smooth=1)
Track(points=[...], smooth=0, closed=True)       # polyline
Track(vectors=[Vec2(50, 0), (0, 80), (-40, 20)], smooth=0)  # relative steps, floats
Track(hexagon)            # live outline; clone() freezes it
Track(sprite)             # live outline of the silhouette (the hurtbox is add_hitbox)
Track(ellipse, floating=True)  # live outline; its position does not hold the traveler
Track.circle(center=(400, 300), radius=120)   # anchored in the world
Track.eight(width=90, height=40)              # floats until someone travels on it

points= are positions in the world (a Vec2 in there is also a position); linking a point with a lambda makes the track follow it. vectors= are steps from the previous point (a turtle path). Both together (or with radius=) raise TypeError. smooth=1 (the default) curves through the points; 0 is a polyline. Track(shape) follows the Shape's live outline; Track(sprite), the painted silhouette. u=0 is at the first vertex (angle 0 on round shapes), counterclockwise.

Ready-made shapes. Centered family (center=): circle, arc, eight, star, spiral, shuttle. Start-point family (p1= / start=): line, wave.

Track.line(length=200)                        # +x, floats
Track.line(length=200, angle=90)              # +y
Track.line(vec=Vec2(120, -40))                # length + direction
Track.line(length=400, angle=-30, p1=(1050, 450))  # planted, u=0 at p1
Track.line(p1=(0, 0), p2=(200, 0))            # two points, anchored
Track.circle(radius=80, center=(400, 300))
Track.arc(radius=80, from_angle=0, to_angle=180)
Track.eight(width=90, height=40)
Track.eight(width=90, height=40, center=(400, 300), floating=True)  # drawn there; the traveler does the eight from where it is
Track.star(points=5, radius=70)
Track.spiral(turns=3, radius=80)
Track.wave(length=200, amplitude=30, waves=3)
Track.wave(length=200, start=(100, 300))
Track.shuttle(length=180)                     # out and back along both sides, closed

Start-point presets plant u=0 with p1= / start=; center= does not apply to them. .center is still the geometric middle. Full table: Presets, below.

Read points of the curve by u: 0 is the start, 1 is the end, and u grows evenly with distance (u=0.5 is halfway along) — to place things along it.

x, y = track.at(0.25)
ang = track.angle_at(0.25)
tx, ty = track.tangent_at(0.25)
pts = track.spaced_points(8)          # closed: the start is not repeated
pts = Track(rail).spaced_points(5)    # open: includes the ends
track.u = 0.5
ship["center"] @= lambda: track.cursor   # places — to travel: move_along

Samples return tuples, not Points, and already include the track's pose (local_at does not). .cursor is the Point at u: linking a center to it places (no sweep against walls).

begin / end trim the stroke: drawing, clicks and collision. Animating end from 0 to 1 “draws” the curve.

ring = Track.circle(center=(400, 300), radius=80, color="gold", line_width=5)
ring.end = 0
tween(ring["end"], 1, time=1.4, ease="ease_out")
# a window that moves around a loop (closed wraps around)
crawl = Track.circle(center=(400, 300), radius=100, color="cyan", line_width=4)
crawl.begin = 0
crawl.end = 0.2

The window does not change the curve: at(u), length and move_along follow the whole curve. Closed with begin > end wraps around the loop; open with begin >= end neither draws nor collides. The stretch of one trip is something else: span= on move_along.

They deform the curve on the object itself and return the Track (chainable).

base = Track(points=[(80, 200), (520, 200)], smooth=0)
base.zigzag(amount=24, waves=6)     # changes this Track, returns self
base.orbit(radius=12, laps=4)
base.wander(amount=10, seed=3)
# clone() first if you want the original straight line

To keep the original, clone() first: the clone freezes the current view (including reversed() and modifiers) into a polyline.

A stroke with line_width collides like a thick line: that makes a curved wall.

wall = Track.arc(
    center=(400, 300), radius=80, from_angle=0, to_angle=90,
    color="gold", line_width=8, group="wall",
)
resolve(player, "wall", bounce=0.0)

The collision is the stroke (line_width thick), trimmed by begin / end. Closed = a ring, not a disk. A filled slice (clicks and collision on the disk): Circle(angle=, spread=). A motion-only track: leave it unregistered (the default).

Constructor

Track() · Track(points=, smooth=, closed=, quality=, line_width=, color=, begin=, end=, floating=, angle=) · Track(vectors=, start=, smooth=, closed=, floating=) · Track(shape, floating=) · Track(center=, radius=, floating=)

Sizes only → floats until move_along (at= picks another starting point for that trip). A placement word given → anchored. An explicit floating= always wins. u=0 at the first vertex (angle 0 on round shapes), counterclockwise. Moving, rotating or scaling the track (center / angle / scale) does not rebuild the points; at(u) already returns the position with the current place and rotation. angle= in the constructor is the initial pose.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
source1stShape or SpriteTrack(hexagon): the track is that Shape's live outline (or the Sprite's silhouette). Anchored (pose linked to the source). floating=True turns off only the position — the source's outline / rotation / scale stay live. clone() freezes it.
pointsname=list of pointsPositions in the world. Each point is copied if it is a tuple, a Point or a Vec2 (where it is now), or linked if it is a function ([(0, 0), lambda: ship.center]); the list itself is fixed (points=lambda: […] raises TypeError). At least 2. Anchored. With linked points, .center is derived (the middle of the points; read-only). A Vec2 here is a position, not a step. floating=True frees the pose from the listed points.
vectorsname=list of Vec2 or (dx, dy)Turtle path: each item is a step from the previous one. Without start= it floats; with start= it is anchored (u=0 at that point). Open. Don't mix with points= / radius=. Don't use center=.
smoothname=number or False10 / False = polyline. 1 = curve. >1 = overshoots the points.
closedname=boolLoop. Default: Track() (= eight) closed; points= / vectors= open.
qualityname="high" or "low""high"Samples per segment. Only if you ask — never picked on its own because there is a link.
center / radiusname=point / numberWith radius=: the circle model (without center= it floats). center= plants the centered presets (circle / arc / star / eight / spiral / shuttle). Don't mix radius= with points= / vectors=. On line / wave / vectors= use p1= / start=.
startname=pointOnly on vectors= (and the Track.wave preset). Plants u=0. Omitted → floats.
floatingname=bool or omittedExplicit always wins. Without it: placement given → anchored; sizes only → floats until it gets a place (linking / writing .center, move_to, move_by), which anchors it. With floating=True moving it does not anchor it.
anglename=degrees0Initial heading (pose). Not part of the local polyline. On line / shuttle, angle= is that heading: the segment is built along +x and rotated, so Track.line(angle=30).angle is 30.
color / visualname=color or VisualStyle. color= sets the stroke. Either one, when you make it, makes the Track visible and puts it on the layer; a style given later (t.color = "white") does not show an invisible Track: write t.visible = True. Track is a Shape: the same .dash / .line_cap / .line_join (strings). scale enlarges the whole drawing, stroke included; to grow only the shape of a circle / arc, change radius.
line_widthname=numberStroke thickness. Also counts as style. Not width= — that is the size of Track.eight.
begin / endname=number 0…10 / 1Window of the stroke (drawing, clicks and collision). Default: the whole path. Outside 0…1 it is clamped. Does not change length / at / move_along.
visiblename=boolFalseLike Point: True moves it up to the layer. Without a style and without this, it stays out of the draw list.
layer / groupname=as for any object on screenAn explicit layer= also registers the Track on the canvas.
Construction models
CallMeaning
Track()The same as Track.eight(). Sizes only — floats.
points=Curve (default smooth=1). Open. Anchored at the points. Positions in the world — a Vec2 is also a position. Linked points: .center is derived (read-only).
points=, smooth=0Polyline.
vectors=Relative steps (Vec2 or (dx, dy)). Open. Without start= it floats. Don't mix with points= / radius=.
Track(shape)Live outline. Anchored. floating=True turns off the position. If the source is destroyed, the trip goes on with the last outline read.
center=, radius=Circle. Anchored only with center= (unless floating= says otherwise).
Presets

They take the same smooth= quality= line_width= color= begin= end= floating= angle= layer= group= as the constructor. Centered family: center=. Start-point family: p1= (line) or start= (wave). A position in the preset → anchored; sizes only → floats; an explicit floating= always wins.

CallMeaning
Track.line(length=, angle=, p1=) · Track.line(vec=, p1=) · Track.line(p1=, p2=)Open segment. smooth=0. Sizes only → floats; p1= plants u=0. p1=/p2= anchors (both required); .center is derived (the midpoint; read-only). length=/angle= or vec= — not both, and don't mix them with p1=/p2=. angle in degrees (0 = +x). Length omitted = a medium size. Don't use center=. Several steps: Track(vectors=[…], smooth=0).
Track.circle(radius=, center=)Closed circle. Without center= it floats. radius omitted = a medium size.
Track.arc(radius=, from_angle=, to_angle=, center=)Open arc. Angles in degrees. Default 0 → 180. Without center= it floats. Curved wall: color= + line_width= + group= / @collide.
Track.eight(width=90, height=40, center=)Closed figure eight. u=0 at the crossing (= center). Without center= it floats. Track() is this.
Track.star(points=5, radius=, inner=, center=)Closed star. points ≥ 3 (the number of tips, not a list). inner omitted = 40% of the radius. Without center= it floats.
Track.spiral(turns=3, radius=, center=)Open spiral. u=0 at the innermost point (= center). Without center= it floats. radius omitted = a medium size.
Track.wave(length=200, amplitude=30, waves=3, start=)Open wave. start= plants u=0. Without start= it floats. Don't use center=.
Track.shuttle(length=, angle=, center=) · Track.shuttle(vec=, center=)A closed 1-D stroke: it goes out to both sides from the center and back. length= is the total width (as in Track.line). Arc length per lap = 2 * length. Without center= it floats. length=/angle= or vec= — not both. loops="forever" does not need yoyo=.
Track reference

Properties

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.centerpointread / writeGeometric middle / pose. Write or link it to move the track without rebuilding the points. On linked points= and on Track.line(p1=, p2=) it is derived (writing raises DerivedAttributeError). On a track that floats for lack of a placement, linking / writing anchors it; with floating=True it does not change is_floating.
.radiusnumberread / writeOnly on the circle / arc model.
.lengthnumberreadTotal length of the curve, in design units. Read-only: to change it, change the shape (radius=, points=…).
.unumber0read / writeParameter 0…1. Writing it moves the cursor.
.begin / .endnumber 0…10 / 1read / writeWindow of the stroke (drawing, clicks and collision). Tween: tween(track["end"], 1, time=1.2). Closed with begin > end: wraps around the loop. Open with begin >= end: does not draw (or collide). The fill disappears while the window is not the whole path. Not the span= of move_along.
.cursorPointreadThe point at u; computed only when you read or link it. ["center"] @= lambda: cursor places — it does not sweep.
.closedboolreadLoop. Read-only.
.is_floatingboolread / writeWhether this track's pose holds the traveler. True: the curve starts where the traveler is (or at at=). Every Track has a real .center — floating is not “no position”. Writing it here (or floating= in the constructor) is your word: nothing else changes it. Without it, a track made without a placement floats until it gets a place (linking / writing .center, move_to, move_by) and then anchors — anything already traveling on it starts following it.
.smooth / .qualitynumber / "high" or "low"read / writeRead and write them. Writing recomputes the curve's points.
.visibleboolFalseread / writeLike Point: True promotes it to the layer; False takes it out of the draw list.

Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
at(u)Parameters: u (0 to 1)(x, y)The point of the curve at u, already with the track's current place and rotation. Does not return a Point.
local_at(u)Parameters: u (0 to 1)(x, y)A sample in local space (no pose).
angle_at(u)Parameters: u (0 to 1)degreesHeading of the tangent. 0 = +x, counterclockwise.
tangent_at(u)Parameters: u (0 to 1)(tx, ty)Unit tangent in the world.

spaced_points(n)Parameters: n (integer)list of (x, y)n points at constant speed (arc length). Closed: the return point is not repeated. Open: includes both ends. Tuples, not Point. A Shape's outline: Track(rail).spaced_points(8).
reversed()No parametersTrack (view)Instant: the same track, traveled backwards. reversed().reversed() is the original. The view has no pose of its own: center, angle, scale, flips and the verbs are the original track's. For this trip only: span=(1, 0).
zigzag(amount=20, waves=6, *, kind="sine")Parameters: amount (number), waves (number), kind ("sine" or "saw")selfMakes it wavy, on the object itself. clone() if you want the smooth copy.
orbit(radius=20, laps=8)Parameters: radius (number), laps (number)selfCoils around the curve. On the object itself.
wander(amount=6, seed=0)Parameters: amount (number), seed (integer)selfA stable random drift. On the object itself.
clone(floating=)Parameters: floating (bool, omitted copies the original)TrackFreezes the current view (including reversed and modifiers) into a polyline. Copies is_floating; clone(floating=True) turns off the pose on the clone.

Functions

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
show_tracks(enabled=True)Parameters: enabled (on, True/False)—A magenta overlay of the active trips and of the still Tracks on a layer. It does not turn on visible. Also collision.show_tracks. Ctrl+Shift+7 (the inspection zoom of Ctrl+Shift+8 does not show the tracks). Off: zero extra work per frame. It is debugging, not game logic — see Debug.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
The stroke thickness is width=line_width=. Track.eight(width=…) is the size of the eight.Track(..., width=)
Track.arc and Circle(angle=, spread=)Track.arc(from_angle=, to_angle=) is the path (it has a direction and collides as a stroke). Circle(angle=, spread=) is the filled slice.the same shape

History

A History keeps the last objects (or positions) you add and drops the oldest on its own — once there are more than max_points= or they are older than duration= seconds. Use it for trails made of pieces (dots, segments), snakes, queues. It does not draw: what shows up are the objects you put in it (add), and what leaves is destroyed. snapshot stores only a position. For a continuous stroke that fades: Contrail.

dots = History(max_points=40, on_leave=lambda dot: dot.dissolve_out(0.3))

def drop_dot():
    dot = dots.add(Circle(center=tip.center, radius=4))
    dot.visual = Halo("cyan")

every(0.05, drop_dot)
History constructor

History(*, max_points=, duration=, on_leave=, destroy_on_leave=True)

The two limits are independent and can be rewritten later. Lowering a limit evicts at once (oldest first, full exit). duration= is checked every frame; with only max_points= (or neither) the History stays idle until add / snapshot / pop / discard / clear.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
max_points=name=int or NoneNoneCapacity. When it overflows, the oldest leaves. To grow the trail: h.max_points += 1.
duration=name=number or NoneNoneThe longest time, in seconds, each thing is kept; the oldest leaves on its own even without a new add. None: no time limit.
on_leave=name=function or Nonelambda d: …A side effect on leaving. One argument: the thing, still alive. It does not replace the destroy. Also h.on_leave = fn. Don't mix it with an on_leave method in a subclass.
destroy_on_leave=name=boolTrueDefault: an Entity it holds is destroyed on leaving (it waits for a dissolve_out / fade_out / implode / burn_out in progress to finish). False: forgets it without destroying it (cards already played). Constructor only; afterwards it is read-only.
Read / write / remove
NameSignatureReturnsMeaning
add(thing)Parameters: thingthingStores the object. On leaving: on_leave, then it is destroyed if it is a live Entity (deferred while dissolve_out / fade_out / implode / burn_out plays). A part of another object and a live value (mouse, Vec2) raise TypeError at once; the same object stored twice raises ValueError (it would be destroyed twice).
snapshot(point) / snapshot(x, y)Parameters: point (point) or x, yPointStores a copy of the position, which follows nothing. Nothing to destroy.
history[i] / [a:b]index / slicevalue / list0 = oldest, -1 = newest. A slice is a copy (not a live view).
.first / .lastanyreadShortcuts for [0] and [-1].
len(history) / for v in history——From oldest to newest.
pop(index=-1)Parameters: index (int)valueTakes it out alive. No on_leave, no destroy — it is yours now.
discard(value)Parameters: valueboolRemoves by identity (not equality). Full exit. No error if it is missing.
clear()No parameters—Everything leaves, from oldest to newest (full exit).
.max_points / .durationint / float / Noneread / writeLive limits. Lowering one evicts at once.
 
segments = History(max_points=100, duration=2.0)

def sample():
    start = segments.last.p2 if segments else tip.center
    segment = segments.add(Line(p1=start, p2=tip.center))
    segment.visual = Laser("red")

every(0.05, sample)

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
add(tip) or add(tip.center) stores the poseadd(tip) makes the History the owner of tip, and it destroys tip on leaving. add(tip.center) raises TypeError — the part belongs to tip. A position: snapshot(tip).an automatic copy
History draws the trailstorage only. A continuous stroke: Contrail. Circles / segments: add(Circle(...)) / add(Line(...)).Track / MotionTrail / .tail
on_leave= on a subclass with def on_leavea TypeError — the callback and the method do not stack.both together
on_leave cancels the destroyan extra. The destroy goes away only with destroy_on_leave=False. A death verb in on_leave finishes before the destroy.a replacement for the destroy
snapshot of a destroyed entity (or of its .center / .p1)a DestroyedError, with the hint to use e.every(...).the last point, silently

Contrail

A Contrail draws a trail: a continuous line through an object's last positions, which can fade from head to tail (fade=). You only say when to store a position — contrail.snapshot(ship), usually with ship.every(0.05, …) — and the stroke updates on its own. It is a History with a stroke, positions only (add raises).

trail = Contrail(max_points=100, duration=2.0, fade=True, ease="ease_out",
                 visual=Laser("red"), line_width=3)
dst.every(0.05, lambda: trail.snapshot(dst))  # stops on destroy; pauses with dst.active = False

# faceted polyline
Contrail(smooth=0, line_join="miter", visual=Laser("red"))

# grows like a snake
trail.max_points += 1

# base alpha (fade multiplies on top of it — head = 0.5, tail → 0)
Contrail(duration=1.0, color=Color("cyan").with_alpha(0.5), fade=True)
Contrail constructor

Contrail(*, max_points=, duration=, fade=, ease=, color=, visual=, line_width=, line_join=, smooth=, on_leave=, layer=)

The same limits as History. A private stroke (not a Track). smooth=1 by default (cubic); smooth=0 = polyline. No stroke= — use color=.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
max_points= / duration=name=int / number / NoneThe same as in History (live; lowering one evicts at once).
fade=name=boolFalseTrue: alpha 0 at the tail → 1 at the head (a multiplier on the color's alpha).
ease=name=name or function"linear"The curve of the fade. Only with fade=True. Default "linear". The same catalog as tween.
color=name=colorgame defaultThe stroke color; e.g. Color("cyan").with_alpha(0.5). Alpha = the 4th channel — there is no alpha=.
visual=name=VisualNoneThe stroke's Visual (e.g. Laser("red")). Mutually exclusive with color= in the constructor, as in Shape.
line_width=name=number1.5Stroke thickness, in design units. Also contrail.line_width = … later.
line_join=name=str"round"The stroke's corners (useful with smooth=0). Default "round". Faceted: "miter". It does not make a curve.
smooth=name=number or False10 / False = polyline. 1 = a Catmull-Rom curve (cubics in the path). >1 = overshoots the points. The same as Track.smooth.
on_leave=name=function or NoneA side effect when the tail recedes (a spark, a sound). The stroke always updates on its own.
layer=name=layer name"default"The stroke's layer: on a layer behind (canvas.layers.create("trail", below="default")) the trail passes behind the ship. Also contrail.layer = … later.
Methods and properties
NameSignatureReturnsMeaning
snapshot(point) / snapshot(x, y)Parameters: Point / (x, y) / GraphicPointAlways stores an unlinked Point. contrail.snapshot(dst) is enough. add raises TypeError.
len / index / iterate / .first / .last——Inherited from History (the values are Points).
.color / .visual / .line_width / .line_join / .line_cap—read / writeRead and change the trail's stroke, as on a Shape.
.smoothnumberread / writeRebuilds the path (cubic or polyline).
.fade / .easebool / callableread / writeRebuild the stroke. ease= requires fade=True.
.max_points / .duration—read / writeThe same as in History.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
Contrail is a Tracka History with a minimal private stroke. No move_along / presets / begin/end.Track(points=…)

Sampling set in the constructordst.every(0.05, lambda: trail.snapshot(dst)) — the rhythm is separate from the storage. The timer belongs to the object being read.sample(...) / record(every=) / Graphic.contrail(...)
The module's every samples the herohero.every(...), which stops on destroy and pauses with active = False. The module's every raises DestroyedError on its next firing and does not pause when the object is parked. A bare every fits mouse or the body of a mode.the framework retiring the timer silently
A teleport continues the stroketrail.clear() together with the new position — otherwise the next sample draws a streak from where it was.the framework guessing the jump was a teleport

Circles / segments in a ContrailHistory with add(Circle(...)) / add(Line(...)).shape_factory= / add on the Contrail

Text

A piece of text on screen — a score, a caption, a title. It stays fixed to the window (HUD) or sits in the world with the objects, depending on how you place it (table below). The box follows the text (or has a fixed width=) and grows downward.

Text("SCORE")                                   # HUD, in the automatic column
st.score = 0
hud = Text("", top_left=(20, 780), font_size=20)
hud["text"] @= lambda: f"Stars {st.score}"
Text("HP", center=ship.center)                  # in the world, moves with the camera
Text("GAME OVER\nPress SPACE", center=(500, 400))
Place withWhere it goes
nothing (just the text)The ui layer, in the automatic column — the same stack as the widgets. stack=False keeps it out of the column.
top_left= / top_center= / top_right=Pins that point of the box; the text grows away from it (always downward) — a new line or a larger font_size does not push the top. With layer left out: the ui layer (and it advances the column). With layer="default": a caption in the world.
center=Without layer=: in the world (default), moves with the camera. With layer="ui": on the window.
box=The box's center at the region's center, the region's width. Out of the column. Prefer canvas.ui_view.

Lines. \n is a hard line break (height = n × the line metric). Without width= the box follows the widest line; with width=, whatever does not fit is cut off (no automatic wrapping). align= aligns each line inside the box and never moves the anchor. The HUD column does not rearrange itself if the number of lines changes after the Text is built.

st.score = 0
score = Text("", top_right=(980, 780), font_size=20)
score["text"] @= lambda: f"{st.score}"
Text("READY", top_left=(20, 720), width=160, background="maroon")
Text("Kills 3\nTime 1:02", top_right=(980, 700), align="left")
Text("HP 100/100", center=ship.center, width=120, align="center")

# follow another object: a lambda in the point (or in one axis)
panel = Rect(center=(500, 300), width=300, height=120, layer="ui")
Text("Menu", top_left=lambda: panel.top_left)
Text("x", top_left=(lambda: mouse.x, 760))
Text constructor

Text(text, top_left=, top_center=, top_right=, center=, box=, width=, align=, layer=, font=, font_size=, color=, background=, glow=, stack=, group=, angle=)

1st: the text, or a field it shows (st["score"]). Leave out center=/layer= → the ui layer + the automatic stack (the same as the widgets'). center= without a layer → the default world layer. A point (top_left= …) on the ui layer also advances the column. There is no x1= / y1= / pos=: the error points to the point.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
text1ststr, field or function"SCORE"The text; or a field (st["score"]), which the Text shows and follows one way only (like t["text"] @= st["score"]: t.text = … raises LinkedAttributeError; to change what shows, change the field); or a function, which links. A number raises an error: write a string (Text(str(n))). Text(st.nickname) is the text as it is now and does not follow; the field is st["nickname"]. Reading t.text gives the text that shows now, a str like any other (it works as a dictionary key, in in, in join), also when it is linked; the link is t["text"] (t["text"] @= …, t["text"].unlink()).
top_left= / top_center= / top_right=name=point(20, 780)Only one. Pins that point of the box (the visual top); the text grows downward and away from it — a new line or a larger font_size does not push the top. With none: the column's stack. layer left out → ui (advances the column); layer="default" → a caption in the world, out of the column. A value is copied; a lambda links, as in Rect(top_left=): top_left=lambda: panel.top_left, or a mixed tuple (lambda: mouse.x, 760) (only x links). A Point you pass is copied. Moving (move_by, move_to, time=, tween, dragging) takes the point along; move_to(x, y) puts the middle of the current string at (x, y). With a linked anchor, moving raises LinkedAttributeError (use t["top_left"].unlink()).
width=name=number120A fixed box. Left out → follows the string. Whatever does not fit is cut off (no wrapping). \n is a hard line break (height = n × the line metric). The column does not rearrange itself if the number of lines changes later.
align=name=str"left""left" / "center" / "right" (or XPos.LEFT / XPos.CENTER / XPos.RIGHT). Aligns each line inside the box (width= or the widest line); never moves the anchor. The default follows the anchor: top_left → "left", top_right → "right", top_center / center= / box= → "center". Any combination works (e.g. a block at top_right= with its lines aligned left).
stack=name=boolTrueFalse: the Text stays out of the HUD's automatic column (useful for an FPS counter). Default True on the HUD.
center=name=point(400, 300)Pose in the world (or on the window if layer="ui") — the center of the box
box=name=Boxcanvas.ui_view.inset(24)The box's center at the region's center (center= on ui), the region's width if left out. Out of the column. Do not mix with center= / top_left= …. Prefer ui_view. box=.
font= / .fontname=str"pixel.ttf"An installed family, or a .ttf / .otf file (found the same way as an image). Left out, it uses ui.font. .font returns the font's name (a string). Assigning it measures the text again. A missing font: a warning and the default one. No bold / italic.
font_size=name=number13Height of the letters, in design units. Left out: the theme's (13 × ui.scale). Takes lambda:.
color=name=color"white"Color of the letters. Later: set_color(…) or .fill = Gradient(…).
angle=name=number0Turn in degrees, around the center of the box. Takes lambda:.
background=name=color"maroon"An opaque plate behind the text, the size of the box.
glow= / .glowname=bool or color or GlowTrueThe only add-on. True / a color / Glow / CheapGlow. No visual (.visual).
.fill / .line—color or GradientGradient("sunset")Fill / outline (a Gradient works)
.top_left / .top_center / .top_right / .center—Pointscore.top_rightPoints of the current box as drawn — turned and scaled about the center (the read already sees the current string). The anchor writes; the others are derived (writing raises an error). rotate_by / scale_by turn about the center and take the anchor along (an anchor linked with a lambda raises an error; force=True unlinks it). Text does not mirror: flip_x / flip_y = True raises an error (mirrored text cannot be read). To follow it: Line(p1=lambda: score.top_right, …).
.box—Boxhud.box.heightA copy of the layout box (to measure it, to place something beside it).

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
Text(…, layer="top") stays fixed to the windowthe "top" layer, which still moves with the camera. HUD: layer="ui", or leave out center=.HUD
align="right" pins the right edgealign= only aligns the lines inside the box. To pin the right edge: top_right=.anchor
Text for the player to type inText only shows. To type: TextInput. A Slider's label is still label= (a string). The automatic column: ui.stack_reset / stack_origin / stack_from / stack_column.an input box

SpatialFx

A SpatialFx is an effect that sits at a place in the world — a campfire, rain over an area, a portal, a jet. Like a Shape, the constructor already puts the effect on screen, and it has a layer, groups, timers, destroy(), and it can collide (by the area it covers). Unlike a Shape, it has no exact outline and cannot be clicked or dragged.

FamilyEffectsPlacement
PointFire, Sparks, GlowSpot, Orb, Sunburst, Starburst, Warp, Portalcenter= and the size in radius= (the jet Fire uses width=)
AreaRainA rectangle: p1= / p2= (opposite corners) or center=, width=, height=
BeamJetA segment: p1= / p2=, or origin= with angle= and length=

Once it is created, you change its parameters by assignment (fire.amount = 2), and they apply on the next frame. To move it, write or link its center: fire.center = (300, 120), fire["center"] @= lambda: torch.center or tween(fire.center, (300, 120), time=1) — SpatialFx has no move_to / rotate_to. They all take soft_edge=: the width of the fading edge, as a fraction of the size (0 = a hard edge; each effect has its own default). Not to be confused with a visual (it paints an object), a Post (the whole screen) or an Impact (a burst that goes away by itself).

Fire(center=(200, 150))
Warp(center=(400, 220), radius=90, color="cyan")
Rain(p1=(300, 250), p2=(700, 550))

Always by name: Fire(200, 150), at= and x= raise TypeError with the right spelling (center=). shape.visual = Rain() and canvas.effects.add(Fire()) also raise TypeError: the effect is in the world as soon as it is created.

Reading the parameters. color= tints the effect; left out, each effect uses its own color (orange fire, blue Warp…). amount= is the strength: 1 is the default, 0 turns it off, 2 is strong. speed= is the pace of the animation: 1 normal, 2 twice as fast, 0 freezes it. center=, radius=, width= and length= are in design units. All of them change later by assignment: fire.amount = 2. The numbers (amount, speed, twist, glow…) also link and tween like radius: fire["amount"] @= lambda: st.heat, tween(fire["amount"], 0, time=1) (that is how an effect fades out or in), or amount=lambda: … when you make it.

Entity

Entity() creates a game object that draws nothing: a wave director, an enemy spawner, a clock. It has everything the other objects have — own fields, timers, mode, groups, on_update — except the drawing. Shape, Sprite and SpatialFx are Entities too; this constructor is the one that does not paint. Like a drawn shape, it lives until destroy() or until the end of the act, with or without a variable: Director() alone on a line is enough.

director = Entity()
director.after(1.5, start_wave, name="wave")

class Director(Entity):
    def setup(self):
        self.wave = 0

    def on_update(self, dt):
        if ready("spawn", 1.2):
            start_wave()
Entity constructor

Entity(layer=, group=)

A name with =: pass it by name.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
layername=str or NoneNoneNone = out of the drawing list (the usual choice here).
groupname=str or list or NoneA tag, or a list of tags. E.g. group="wasp".
 
class Spawner(Entity):
    def setup(self):
        self.timer = 0

spawner = Spawner(group="spawners")
# No drawing (a plain Entity): only timers, mode and on_update.
# group lets you find them all with group["spawners"].
Entity reference

Properties

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.layer / .groupstr"hud"read / write.layer (str or None), .group (write a str or a list; reads a read-only frozenset — .group.add raises AttributeError, use tag / untag). The same as on every object on screen.
activeboolFalseread / writeParks it: hides and pauses it. With no drawing, visible hardly matters. To remove it: destroy().
