Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
.slide_along(velocity)Parameters: velocity (Vec2)Vec2Projects the velocity onto the tangent (walking / sliding on a slope).

Walked off the platform or jumped → the side goes away at once. Coyote time and jump buffering are your own timers on top of it (recently). touching_contacts can hold more than one item (wall + floor in a corner).

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
@collide(hero, "block") to know which block the hero stands ontouching_contacts (the c.other of the "bottom" contact): it comes from the position already resolved and is steady at any frame rate. @collide on a resolve() pair does not flicker while the body is still, but at the seam between two blocks, with uneven frames, a round body can enter and leave the next block for a few frames.the enter/exit of @collide per block
A sensor / pickup shows up in touching_*never the case: @collide without resolve() detects overlap, but it does not become a floor.a sensor contact
touching_contacts is this frame's contactthe previous frame (like touching_sides). To decide in the same frame, use @collide_stay with info.side, before the automatic resolve.the current frame
On a slope, turn the hero with .anglea turn of the collider, which then stumbles. Use tilt — the drawing only, with hitbox_anchor="bottom". See Tilt..angle

Floor ahead

object.floor_below(dx=) returns the floor the object would stand on after walking dx, or None if it would fall. It is the platformer's ledge: the enemy that turns back before falling, the hero teetering on the edge. It is a question for a world with a floor (collision.floor = True); in a world without one it warns once.

collision.floor = True              # a world with a floor (A world with a floor)
resolve(enemy, "ground", bounce=0.0)

def update(dt):
    ahead = enemy.hitbox.box.width * st.dir
    if "bottom" in enemy.touching_sides and not enemy.floor_below(dx=ahead):
        st.dir = -st.dir            # the toe reached the ledge: turn back
    enemy.move_by(60 * st.dir * dt, 0)

standing_on = hero.floor_below()    # which floor I am on (or None in the air)
if not hero.floor_below(dx=2 * st.dir):
    hero.play("teetering")          # one more step and it falls
floor_below reference
MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
floor_below(dx=0, depth=None, group=None)Parameters (by name): dx (signed number, + = right), depth (≥ 0), group (tag or list)the object that serves as floor, or NoneWalks dx in short steps (climbs slopes up to 45°, stops at a wall) and asks whether there is a floor below. Read-only: it does not move, does not use up the pending movement, does not enroll anyone.

The same rules as the physics. The hitbox decides (not the drawing), a floor is a "bottom" contact (±45°, the same as touching_sides), and a drop deeper than depth is a fall. Without depth, the reach that resolve() steps down by itself applies (16 units): it walks down a smaller step; on a bigger one, the body falls. So None means "the physics will let it fall". depth only applies to steps and vertical drops: a slope up to 45° is floor with any depth. A box resting on just its corner is still on the floor; a circle starts to roll once the contact leaves the 45°.

What counts as floor. Without group=, whatever the body resolves against (resolve(body, …), with its only=): a coin, a sensor and an enemy with only @collide do not count. group="ground" names the floor — that is how a critter with no resolve(), moved by script, asks. With neither, it raises ValueError listing both ways out.

What dx asks. One number covers the cases: dx=0 is the floor right now; a small dx is "do I fall on the next step?"; dx = width is "has the toe gone past the ledge?" (the enemy that turns back); dx = width / 2 is "has the middle gone past?". Use the hitbox's width (hitbox.box.width), not the drawing's (box.width includes the PNG's transparent margin). A wall in the way is not a ledge: the answer is the floor where the walk stopped. Walls are "left" / "right" in touching_sides.

With show_colliders, each question shows where the walk ended: magenta = found a floor, red = would fall.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
Compare x with the edge of the block underfootfloor_below: two blocks side by side do not turn into a "ledge" at the seam, and a slope does not turn into a cliff.c.other.box.right
A test point with collision.query_point in front of the footenough for a rectangle on flat ground. floor_below uses the whole hitbox and the physics' floor rule (slope, circle, step).the same question
floor_below() for "am I on the ground?""bottom" in touching_sides. floor_below() finds a floor up to 16 units below — also at the start of a jump.grounded

Manual resolution

For when the automatic resolve is not enough: a dash, a kinematic controller, a decision inside the collision function. Five tiers, one recipe — detect → separate position → separate velocity — with the same mass_a/mass_b/bounce=.

TierCallWhen
1resolve(a, b, bounce=)A standing registration — the everyday tier
2shape.resolve_now(target, bounce=)Detects + resolves now; returns a list of CollisionInfo
3info.resolve(bounce=)Inside the collision function — a pair already detected
4info.push_apart() / info.bounce_apart(bounce=)Advanced — applies with explicit masses, not necessarily .mass
5info.mtv_split() / info.velocity_split()Advanced — tuples only, you decide what "apply" means

The path for 95% of scripts: register once, or resolve on your own when the moment calls for it.

# Declarative (the engine runs it by itself):
resolve(player, "walls", bounce=0.0)

# Manual in update — before Scena checks the frame's collisions:
for info in player.resolve_now("walls", bounce=0.0):
    if info.side == "bottom":
        grounded = True

# Manual inside the collision function — a conditional resolve:
@collide_stay(player, "walls")
def touch(me, other, info):
    if not player.dashing:
        info.resolve(bounce=0.0)

The standing registration resolve(a, b) follows the path of the frame's movement. resolve_now / info.resolve only push an already overlapping pair apart along the shortest way that separates them (the MTV) — they do not look at the path.

An escape hatch: make-believe masses (not the bodies' real .mass) and partial effects that resolve() cannot express by itself.

# Tier 4 — applies right away, with masses chosen on the spot:
@collide(player, boulder)
def hit(me, other, info):
    info.push_apart(mass_a=1.0, mass_b=10.0)               # position only
    info.bounce_apart(mass_a=1.0, mass_b=10.0, bounce=0.3)  # + velocity

# Tier 5 — tuples only: you decide what "apply" means —
# here, half a push, for a softer bump:
@collide(player, cloud)
def hit(me, other, info):
    (dxa, dya), (dxb, dyb) = info.mtv_split(mass_a=1.0, mass_b=1.0)
    player.move_by(dxa * 0.5, dya * 0.5)
    cloud.move_by(dxb * 0.5, dyb * 0.5)

Here mass_a= / mass_b= do not need to be a.mass / b.mass: they are for a push that is just for effect, without touching the real mass. Without an explicit slop=, mtv_split / velocity_split make the bodies touch exactly (no gap); push_apart / bounce_apart (and resolve) leave the small gap that keeps stay from jittering.

Resolution methods on CollisionInfo
MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
shape.resolve_now(target, bounce=)Parameters: target (object or group name), bounce (number, optional)list of CollisionInfoDetects and resolves now, without waiting for the frame's automatic check.
info.resolve(bounce=)Parameters: bounce (number, optional)—push_apart + (if bounce is given) bounce_apart. Left out = position only, like resolve(a, b) without bounce=.
info.push_apart(mass_a=, mass_b=)Parameters: mass_a (number), mass_b (number)—mtv_split + move_by on both bodies. Without explicit masses, it uses a.mass/b.mass.
info.bounce_apart(mass_a=, mass_b=, bounce=1.0)Parameters: mass_a (number), mass_b (number), bounce (number)—velocity_split + writes .vel. Here bounce is already 1.0 by default (unlike resolve(), which skips the velocity when it is left out).
info.mtv_split(mass_a=1, mass_b=1, slop=0)Parameters: mass_a (number), mass_b (number), slop (number)two offsets (dx, dy)Only the push tuple along the shortest way apart — no move_by. slop: how much of the overlap is left undone (0 = they touch exactly). A mass <= 0 raises an error.
info.velocity_split(mass_a=, mass_b=, bounce=, vel_a=, vel_b=)Parameters: mass_a (number), mass_b (number), bounce (number), vel_a (Vec2), vel_b (Vec2)two Vec2Only computes the two objects' new velocities after the impact — without writing .vel. vel_a/vel_b are required here (it does not read .vel by itself).
info.reflect_velocity(velocity, restitution=1)Parameters: velocity (Vec2), restitution (number)Vec2Reflects a velocity about normal. The mass_b=STATIC case of velocity_split — it still exists, but it is not the recommended primitive for a moving body.

Queries

Ask the system on the spot, without waiting for a collision function to fire: who is at this point, in this circle, in this cone, in front of this ray.

collision already exists after from scena import * — like canvas or clock. You do not build it. It is not a Shape. Scena checks collisions by itself every frame; the script does not need to call anything for that.

hits = collision.query_point(mouse)
near = collision.query_circle(mouse, radius=80)
enemies = collision.query_circle(mouse, radius=80, group="enemy")
seen = collision.query_sector(guard, radius=300, spread=60, group="enemies")
wedge = Circle(center=lambda: guard.center, radius=300, spread=60, use_center=True)
wedge["angle"] @= lambda: guard.angle
hit = collision.raycast(player, p2=mouse)
blocked = collision.raycast(hero, p2=enemy, ignore=enemy)
if hit:
    body, t, point = hit

info = test_collision(player, door)
victims = collision.query_shape(explosion, group=["ships", "asteroids"])
nearby = player.collides_with(group="enemy")

Who a query sees. Without group= (or with group=ANYTHING): only what is already enrolled (collidable, @collide, resolve, on_collide) — bodies, not parts. With group= (a tag, group['name'], a list / tuple / set): the members of that group, enrolled or not, without enrolling anyone. A Graphic at the origin is the one asking and is never a hit; ignore= adds to it (a body, a tag, group['name'], or a list).

collision reference
MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
collision.query_point(x, y=None, *, group=, ignore=)Parameters: x (a point, or the number x with y); group, ignore (optional)listThe objects whose hitbox contains the point. A point (query_point(mouse)) or two numbers. Not contains_point (drawing / click).
collision.query_circle(x, y=None, radius=None, *, group=, ignore=)Parameters: x (a point, or the number x with y); radius (number ≥ 0); group, ignore (optional)listThe objects that overlap the circle. query_circle(x, y, radius) or query_circle(p, radius=80). After a point, radius= goes by name. A negative radius raises ValueError.
collision.query_sector(origin, angle=, radius=, spread=, group=, ignore=)Parameters: origin (point); angle (degrees, optional); radius and spread (numbers ≥ 0); group, ignore (optional)listWhat overlaps a sector (a radar). spread=60 is the whole opening (±30). With angle= left out, it uses a Graphic's .angle (on a Sprite that is already where the art points). Without a Graphic, angle= is required. spread=0 becomes just the sector's middle line: it returns every object that line touches. spread=360 is query_circle. Above 360 raises ValueError. Registration order, not sorted by distance. Blocked sight: raycast afterwards. Draw the same slice: Circle(center=, radius=, angle=, spread=) (use_center starts out True; False is the chord segment).
collision.query_shape(shape, group=)Parameters: shape (object), group (str or list)listWhat overlaps shape's geometry. group=: a tag, a list / set (OR), group['name'], ANYTHING. The probe itself is not a hit.
shape.collides_with(group=)Parameters: group (str or list)listA shortcut: query_shape(self, group=).
test_collision(a, b)Parameters: a (object), b (object)CollisionInfo, or NoneA one-shot test between two targets.
collision.raycast(p1, p2= / vec= / angle= length=)Parameters: p1 (point); one end: p2 (point), or vec (offset), or length with an optional angle; group, ignore (optional)tuple, or NoneThe first object the segment hits. A second argument without a name raises TypeError — the end goes by name: p2=, vec=, or angle= and length=. With angle= left out, it uses the Graphic's .angle. vec= does not take a Point, a Graphic or mouse. The end target counts, unless it is in ignore=. (object, t, point) or None: the object hit; t from 0 to 1, the fraction of the segment up to the impact (0 = it starts inside); the point of impact.

What collides

What enters the system (collidable) and with which shape. The hitbox is not the drawing.

ball.collidable = True
wasp.collidable = False   # opt-out, even with @collide("wasp", …)

collidable is a property on Shape, Sprite and SpatialFx — it turns the hitbox on in the registry (queries, a target of ANYTHING, debug outlines). It is not a method of collision: it lives on the body. Default False. @collide, resolve and on_collide = fn enroll by themselves. False takes it out of the system (and keeps it out) — even with @collide("wasp", …) — until it goes back to True. Two bodies with only the flag are not tested against each other every frame; name the pair or use on_collide / ANYTHING.

A point of a Shape (c.center, rope.p2, a vertex) is not an object that collides: collidable = True, on_collide, @collide and resolve with it raise TypeError. Collide with its owner (@collide(rope, wall); info.point says where it touched), test a point (wall.contains_point(rope.p2)) or create an object that follows it: tip = Point(lambda: rope.p2) — that one is yours; destroy it when you like. Queries (test_collision, collides_with) take the point.

BodyWhat collides
ShapeThe model's geometry (circle, rectangle, polygon…).
TrackA row of thin rectangles along the stroke, as thick as line_width. Closed = a ring (empty hole), not a disc. begin/end trim the stroke that collides.
SpriteThe computed hitbox (the body): shape and art chosen by hitbox_shape= / hitbox_source=, frozen while animating. See Sprite hitbox.
Sprite partsprite.add_hitbox(group=…) — an extra collider, detection only, that follows the drawing and answers for the groups it claims. See Parts.
SpatialFxThe domain (orb, area, beam) — not the glow.

It does not exist on a Widget, a Text, or on an Entity() with no drawing. A parallax / ui layer: TypeError. To see the outlines: collision.show_colliders() — pairs in resolve() in gold.

Collider

A Collider joins several shapes into a single body for collision — a boss made of a torso and a head, a ship of several pieces. @collide(body, "bolt") fires once for the body, and the function's me is the Collider, not the piece that was hit. The pieces still draw and move each on its own; the Collider only joins them for collision. A single shape does not need a Collider: name it directly in @collide / resolve.

torso = Rect(center=(500, 300), width=80, height=120)
head = Circle(center=(500, 390), radius=30)
body = Collider([torso, head])

@collide(body, "bolt")
def on_hit(me, other, info):
    other.destroy()

Collider(shapes)

Parameter / fieldPassTypeMeaning
shapes1stlist of Shapes[torso, head]The pieces of the body. body.shapes reads the ones still alive (a destroyed piece leaves the list).
on_collide / on_collide_stay / on_collide_exit—function or NoneThe same three phases as in Detect, on the whole body: body.on_collide = lambda me, other, info: … reacts to any enrolled object.

Weak spot: a piece that is also a body. A piece can be, besides a part of the Collider, a body of its own — with collidable = True, or because a rule names its group. They are two separate outlines: the rule for the piece's group sees the piece, and the rule for the body sees the body.

torso = Rect(center=(500, 300), width=80, height=120, group="weak_spot")
head = Circle(center=(500, 390), radius=30)
boss = Collider([torso, head])

@collide("bolt", "weak_spot")            # a shot in the torso: double damage
def on_weak_spot(shot, piece):
    shot.destroy()

boss.on_collide = lambda me, other, info: …   # a shot anywhere on the boss

The body never collides with its own pieces (nor pushes them in a resolve), and two pieces of the same Collider that are also bodies (two weak spots) do not collide with each other. A rule with ANYTHING sees both bodies: a shot in the torso is two contacts, one with the torso and one with the boss — name the group to count it once. In queries, the Collider comes before the pieces that are also bodies: collision.query_point (and query_circle, query_sector, query_shape) lists the boss first, and collision.raycast returns the boss when the ray enters both at the same point; raycast(…, group="weak_spot") returns the torso. The order of the lines changes none of this.

Where else to look — Move · React · Geometry

Geometry

Geometry math: vectors (Vec2), where two outlines cross, and point functions — distance, heading, midpoint, the nearest one. Angles in degrees. Math on values (remap, blend, chase, roll) is in Utilities.

Vector → Vec2
Outlines crossing → Crossings
distance / heading / closest_point → Points

Vec2

A Vec2 is an arrow: a displacement (dx, dy) or a velocity, with a length and a direction. You can add it to another, multiply it by a number, rotate it. Angles in degrees (0 = to the right).

v = Vec2(1, 0)
w = vec_from_angle(90, length=200)
a1 = v + w          # another Vec2
a2 = w - v          # another Vec2
a3 = w * 0.5        # another Vec2, half as long
a4 = w / 2          # another Vec2 (divided by 2)
ship.move_by(angle=w.angle, distance=w.length)

Changing the length and heading of an existing Vec2. .length and .angle are computed from .x / .y: read-only (v.length = 5 raises an error that shows the right form). To set a length and a heading, build the arrow with vec_from_angle(heading, length) and copy it into v with <<. v stays the same object, so whatever kept it (another object, a list, a formula that reads v) sees the new values. v = vec_from_angle(…), on the other hand, only makes the name v point to another Vec2; whatever kept the old one does not see the change. << is in Link.

v = Vec2(3, 4)                      # length 5, heading ≈ 53°
v << vec_from_angle(30, 10)         # heading 30°, length 10: x ≈ 8.66, y = 5
v << vec_from_angle(v.angle, 2)     # changes only the length (heading stays 30°)
v << vec_from_angle(90, v.length)   # changes only the heading (length stays 2)
Vec2 reference

Properties

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.x / .ynumber1read / writeThe components: how far the arrow goes in x and in y.
.length / .anglenumber200readLength and heading in degrees (0 = +x, from −180 exclusive to 180: an arrow pointing left reads 180), computed from .x / .y. To change them on v itself: v << vec_from_angle(heading, length) (only the length: v << vec_from_angle(v.angle, n); only the heading: v << vec_from_angle(degrees, v.length)). For a new Vec2: .normalize() * n (or cap it with .clamp_length) and .rotate(degrees).

Methods

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
Vec2(x, y)Parameters: x (number), y (number)Vec2Constructor.
vec_from_angle(angle, length=1, reference_vec=None)Parameters: angle (number), length (number), reference_vec (Vec2 or pair)Vec2Degrees. 0 = +x. With reference_vec, the angle counts from its direction (vec_from_angle(90, reference_vec=front) = 90° to the left of front). To move: move_by(angle=, distance=).
+ / -Parameters: other (another Vec2)Vec2Adds / subtracts another vector (or an (x, y) pair). v += w and v -= w change v itself. A Point is a place, not a displacement: v + p is the moved point (a Point), and v - p, v += p, v -= p raise TypeError (the vector between two points is p - q).
* / /Parameters: numberVec2Multiplies / divides by a scalar. Vec2 on the left: v * 2, v / 2. v *= 2 and v /= 2 change v itself, like +=. A True / False is not a number: v * True raises.
.dot(other)Parameters: other (Vec2)numberDot product: positive if the arrows point the same way, 0 if they are perpendicular, negative if opposite.
.normalize()No parametersVec2Same heading, length 1.
.rotate(angle)Parameters: angle (number)Vec2Rotates by degrees (counterclockwise).
.lerp(other, t)Parameters: other (Vec2), t (number)Vec2Blends with other: t=0 gives this vector, t=1 gives other, 0.5 the middle. Outside 0–1 it keeps going along the line (no clamping). There is also the lerp function.
.distance(other)Parameters: other (Vec2 or point)numberDistance. Same metric as distance (Point, tuple, Graphic, …).
.reflect(normal)Parameters: normal (Vec2)Vec2Reflects about the normal. The same as .reflect_about.
.cross(other)Parameters: other (Vec2)numberCross product in the plane: positive if other is to the left of this arrow (counterclockwise), negative if to the right.
.project_onto(onto)Parameters: onto (Vec2)Vec2Projection onto onto.
.reflect_about(normal)Parameters: normal (Vec2)Vec2Bounce off a surface with that normal: Vec2(1, -1).reflect_about(Vec2(0, 1)) → (1, 1).
.perp_left() / .perp_right()No parametersVec2Perpendicular to the left / to the right.
.clamp_length(min_length, max_length)Parameters: min_length (number), max_length (number)Vec2Same heading, length held between min_length and max_length: vel.clamp_length(0, 300) caps the speed at 300.
.to_tuple()No parameters(x, y)A pair of numbers. Also x, y = v (a snapshot of the current value). v[0] raises TypeError: use v.x.

Crossings

The points where the outlines of two shapes cross, as (x, y) tuples. It does not tell you whether one shape is inside the other (for that, @collide). To link a point to a crossing (@= or lambda: in the constructor), use intersection.

The list, now. Empty if the outlines do not meet.

hits = intersections(line, circle)
for x, y in hits:
    Circle(center=(x, y), radius=6, color="red")

hit = min(hits, key=lambda p: distance(line.p1, p)) if hits else None

intersection always returns a point, so it works in a constructor lambda: — here, the chord: the segment between the two crossings. To hide the chord when there are not 2 crossings, link visible with @=.

c1 = Circle(center=(400, 400), radius=120)
c2 = Circle(center=(520, 400), radius=90)

chord = Line(
    p1=lambda: intersection(c1, c2, 0),
    p2=lambda: intersection(c1, c2, 1),
)

chord["visible"] @= lambda: len(intersections(c1, c2)) == 2
Signatures
MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
intersections(a, b)Parameters: a (shape), b (shape)list of pointsWhere the outlines cross now. [] if nowhere.
intersection(a, b, i=0)Parameters: a (shape), b (shape), i (integer)point (x, y)Crossing number i, for @= / the constructor. If there is none, it returns a point near both shapes instead of raising. i < 0 → ValueError.
What goes in / order / what intersection returns
TopicRule
AcceptedLine, Circle, Ellipse, Rect, Square, Concave, Polygon, RegularPolygon, Triangle, Box. Any other type (Point, Track, Sprite) → TypeError.
OutlineLine = the segment p1→p2 (thickness ignored). Circle = the full circle (arc ignored). Ellipse = the whole outline, with rotation. An ellipse flattened to zero = the segment of its major axis. Box / n-gon = its edges (corner_radius ignored). Concave = the box with its curve, as chords within 0.01 units of it.
OrderWith a Line: along it. Two circles: left → right of the line through the centers. If the first is a Circle / Ellipse: along it, from its local +x, in the direction of rotation. Otherwise: along the first.
How manyEllipse × circle or ellipse: up to 4 points. A tangent counts as 1.
What intersection returnshits[i] if it exists; otherwise the last crossing (at a tangent, 0 and 1 give the same point); otherwise a point near both shapes.

A circle inside a square, not touching its outline → []. This is not @collide nor CollisionInfo.points. It does not return a Point. Point / Track raise TypeError. A point on the body: closest_point.

Points

Distance, heading, midpoint, nearest item, projection onto the body. (x, y) tuples — they do not create a Point. point + (dx, dy) returns a new Point (place, not travel).

p = middle_point(a, b)
d = distance(hero, enemy_ship)
hero.angle = heading(hero, enemy_ship)
target = nearest(player, group["wasp"])
dot.center << closest_point(planet, mouse)
shot = Sprite("laser.png", center=ship.center + (0, 28))
beneath = ship.center - (0, 20)

Point. Where the API asks for a place, a point can be a Point, a Vec2, (x, y), a Graphic (its .center) or mouse. Wherever the API expects a place — move_to, center=, about=, snapshot, closest_point, pan_to, query_point, raycast, a tween of a point, move_along(at=), iris center= — any of these works. This copies the position now. To follow it: Circle(center=lambda: mouse) or center @= mouse. A displacement (move_by, pan_by, Track's vec= / vectors=) refuses a place. Graphic and SpatialFx have no .x / .y — the position is .center.

Helpers
MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
middle_point(p1, p2, weight=0.5)Parameters: p1 (point), p2 (point), weight (number)point (x, y)An (x, y) tuple. Point, Vec2, tuple, Graphic or mouse.
distance(p1, p2)Parameters: p1 (point), p2 (point)numberEuclidean distance (≥ 0). Also p1.distance(p2) on a Point (and a Vec2).
heading(origin, target)Parameters: origin (point), target (point)numberHeading in degrees (0 = +x, from −180 exclusive to 180: pointing left reads 180), from origin to target. Also p1.heading(p2) on a Point.
nearest(origin, items, *, within=, where=)Parameters: origin (point), items (list), within (number), where (function)the item, or NoneThe item in items nearest to origin. Details in nearest reference, below.
closest_point(shape, p)Parameters: shape (shape), p (point)point (x, y)The point of the filled body nearest to p, always (x, y). Details in closest_point reference, below.
point + (dx, dy)(dx, dy) or Vec2PointTranslation. Also (dx, dy) + point. point - (dx, dy) goes the other way. point - other is the Vec2 between the two. point + other raises TypeError — for the midpoint, use middle_point. The result does not enter the game.
point += (dx, dy)—errorTypeError, on purpose: += would place the object straight at the spot, passing through walls. To travel: move_by. To place: center = center + (dx, dy).
point == other—True/FalseOn a Point, == compares the object, not the position: c.center == (400, 120) is always False, and two different Points at the same place are not equal either (Scena warns in both cases). Same position: distance(c.center, (400, 120)) == 0, or < 1 if the movement does not land exactly. Same object: a is b. On a Vec2 or a tuple, == compares the position.
shape.contains_point(x, y=None)Parameters: x (a point, or the number x with y)True/FalseDoes this object contain the point (in the world)? The drawing — Click / drag. It is not closest_point nor query_point. An object on the "ui" layer under a camera: pointer_hover.
box.contains_point(x, y=None)Parameters: x (a point, or the number x with y)True/FalseTrue if the point is inside this box. A Box is only an area: it does not receive clicks. To find the square of a board: grid.cell_at — Place.
heading reference

heading(origin, target)

Parameters: origin (point), target (point). Returns number (degrees).

The heading from origin to target — the angle to point from origin toward target. Assign it to .angle.

hero.angle = heading(hero, enemy_ship)
hero.angle = hero.center.heading(enemy_ship.center)  # same value
TopicRule
origin · targetWhere you look from and where you look to. The order matters: swapping them turns the heading by 180°.
What goes inPoint, Vec2, (x, y), Graphic, mouse — the same as for distance / nearest.
Same placeSame place → 0.
Sprite.angle is already a heading in the world (art_angle goes into the drawing). Do not add art_angle again.
nearest reference

nearest(origin, items, *, within=None, where=None)

Parameters: origin (point), items (list), within (number), where (function). Returns the item, or None.

Which item in the list is nearest to the origin. It returns the item itself — not a new Point.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
origin1stpoint(400, 300)Point, Vec2, (x, y), mouse, or anything with .center / .x/.y (Shape, Sprite).
items2nditerablegroup["wasp"]A list, a tuple, group["wasp"], poly.points, … Items with no position are skipped.
within=name=number or None200Maximum distance (inclusive). Leave it out = no limit. Negative → error.
where=name=function (True/False) or Nonelambda w: w.hp > 0A function that takes each item and returns True/False. Only the items that get True count.

A tie: the first one. Empty / nothing within within → None. For a named fleet, prefer group["wasp"].nearest(…) (same metric; it takes within= and where=).

target = nearest(player.center, group["wasp"])
snap = nearest(mouse, poly.points)
coin = nearest(player.center, coins, within=40)
foe = group["wasp"].nearest(player.center, within=200, where=lambda w: w.hp > 0)
closest_point reference

closest_point(shape, p)

Parameters: shape (shape), p (point). Always returns a point (x, y).

The nearest point on the filled body. Inside → the point itself (except for Line). To follow the pointer: dot["center"] @= lambda: closest_point(planet, (mouse.x, mouse.y)) or, in update, dot.center << closest_point(…), which copies the point into dot.center on that frame (place) — see Mouse.

dot["center"] @= lambda: closest_point(planet, (mouse.x, mouse.y))

# or in update:
def update(dt):
    dot.center << closest_point(planet, (mouse.x, mouse.y))

d = distance(player.center, closest_point(wall, player.center))
TopicRule
shape · pThe Shape to search and the reference point. Accepted Shapes: the same as in Crossings; any other type → TypeError.
InsideDisc / box / polygon → p. The circle's center → (cx + r, cy).

heading is not Handle.heading (how far the tween moved this frame) nor Vec2.angle_to (the angle between two arrows). nearest returns an item (a target, a vertex, …). closest_point returns a point on the shape. contains_point is True/False on the drawing (a click), not on the hitbox — Click / drag. To rank items: sorted(items, key=lambda p: distance(origin, p)).

Where else to look — Place · Collision · Draw · Utilities

UI

Interface controls — buttons, sliders, check boxes and text boxes, lists, menus — fixed to the window, above the game and out of the camera's reach. Without a position, they stack in a column together with the HUD Texts.

All widgets → Widgets
Stack in a column → Column
Button / Slider / CheckBox / TextInput / DropDown / Menu → the sections that follow
Extra space in the stack → ui.gap
Next column → ui.stack_column

Widgets

Widgets are the interface controls — Slider, Button, CheckBox, TextInput, DropDown — drawn on the window, above the game, without following the camera. They are for settings and tools (volume, options, the player's name).

Each widget is tied to a value: its 1st argument, an st field written with brackets (Slider(st["volume"])). Without brackets, st.volume is the current number, and the widget raises an error that shows the fix. The two move together both ways — moving the control writes the value, and writing the value in code (st.volume = 0.2) moves the control. Without top_left=, widgets stack in a column in the corner of the window, together with the HUD Texts. ui.scale and ui.font change the size and the font of all of them. Menu is something else: a question in the middle of the screen, outside the column. A button made from your own art: SpriteButton.

ui.scale = 0.85
ui.font = "Menlo"
st.volume = 0.5
st.mute = False
Text("Volume")
Slider(st["volume"], label="Volume", max_value=1)   # range 0…1
CheckBox(st["mute"], label="Mute")
Button(label="Reset", on_click=reset)
ui reference

PropertyType (typical value)Read/WriteMeaning
.data / .valueAttribute or numberslider.dataread / write.data is the tied Attribute; .value is its value now. To show the value in a Text, link to the Attribute: hud["text"] @= lambda: f"{st.volume:.2f}".
visibleboolFalseread / writeFalse hides it: not drawn and gets no clicks. To show it turned off (dimmed, not responding): enabled = False.
pointer_hoverboolTruereadThis widget is the hover target (a widget wins over a Shape or Sprite under it). See Hover.
pointer_pressedboolTruereadPressed on this widget, still held and with the pointer over it. The same rule as for Shapes and Sprites; a turned-off widget never reads True.
on_hover / on_hover_exitfunction or Nonelambda w: …read / writeThe pointer came in / went out. fn(widget) or fn(). The same as @hover / @hover_exit.
group=str"opts"constructorWidgets are Entities. group["opts"].visible / .destroy() works on widgets and HUD Text together.
destroy()method—Takes it out of the game. When the last live item of the current column goes, the cursor goes back to the top of that column.
.boxBoxslider.box.top_rightreadA copy of the widget's rectangle on the window. To put something next to it: ui.stack_origin(slider.box.top_right + (16, 0)).

If the widget's Attribute is linked to a formula (st["volume"] @= …), the formula is in charge: dragging or clicking changes nothing. Changing ui.scale after the widgets are created does not rearrange the column. See Column.

Column

Without top_left=, widgets and HUD Text stack in a column, top to bottom, from the top-left corner of the window. ui.stack_origin / stack_from / stack_reset change where the column goes on; ui.gap() opens a space; ui.stack_column() starts another column beside it. Each item's position is computed when it is created.

st.volume = 0.5
st.mute = False
Text("Volume")
Slider(st["volume"], label="Volume", max_value=1)

ui.stack_column()
Button(label="Another column")

ui.stack_origin(400, 700)
Button(label="Absolute column")

ui.stack_from(hud)
CheckBox(st["mute"], label="Mute")

ui.stack_reset()
Text("Back at the top")
Methods on ui

ui.stack_reset() · ui.stack_origin(x, y) · ui.stack_from(item) · ui.stack_column()

Layout at construction. The next item created without top_left= uses the column; an explicit top_left= still advances the cursor.

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
ui.stack_reset()No parameters—The next item created without top_left= goes back to the default origin: (20, height − 40), with the height from init. Clears a pending ui.gap.
ui.stack_origin(x, y)Parameters: x, y (numbers) or a point—Visual top-left corner of the next item created without top_left= (like move_to: (x, y) or a point, e.g. slider.box.top_right + (16, 0)). No space before it. Starts another column at this point. Clears a pending ui.gap.
ui.stack_from(item)Parameters: item (widget or Text)—Goes on below the item's box. Applies the theme's spacing. Clears a pending ui.gap.
ui.stack_column()Parameters: gap= optional—Same visual top, x past the column. See ui.stack_column.
ui.gap()No parameters—Adds one extra theme space. See ui.gap.

Text(..., center=) and stack=False take no place in the column (FPS / SCENA WARNING / Menu). Destroying the last live item of the current column sends the cursor back to the top. Destroying only some of them does not. Changing ui.scale after building does not rearrange.

Button

An interface button with a caption: clicking calls the on_click function — on release, with the pointer still over it; releasing outside the button cancels the click. To turn an option on / off, use CheckBox; for a button made from your own art, SpriteButton.

The function can take nothing, or take the button itself — it gets the button when it asks for a parameter with no default value. That is why the same function serves a button and a Shape (@click(btn, shape)), and why lambda f=f: … or save_game(then=None) do not get the button. Optional: tied to an Attribute, the button writes value_on while it is held and value_off on release — a "hold to fire".

st.firing = False
Button(label="Reset", on_click=reset)
Button(st["firing"], label="Fire")      # st.firing is True while the button is held

Name without =: 1st, in order. Name with =: by name.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
cell1stfieldOptional (left out: no field; None raises). It follows the button: value_on while held, value_off on release (it is not a toggle — for on/off use CheckBox). Destroyed with the mouse button held (or by a change_act in between), it also writes value_off, with no click: st.firing is not stuck at True. E.g. Button(st["firing"], …).
labelname=str"Button"Text written on the button.

SpriteButton

A game button made from your own art (PNG / JPG / Sheet). The behavior comes built in: it grows and brightens on hover, shrinks and darkens when pressed, clicks on release over it, turns gray when turned off. It is a Sprite (layer ui by default): play, .glow, fade_out… work. For tool buttons (settings, debugging), use Button.

st.coins = 0
start_btn = SpriteButton("button.png", center=(400, 300), label="Play",
                     on_click=start_game, click_sound="click.wav")
shop_btn = SpriteButton("button.png", center=(400, 200), label="Shop", breathe=True)
shop_btn["enabled"] @= lambda: st.coins >= 10    # gray until you have 10 coins
start_btn.label_text.glow = True                  # the label's Text: fine control
# Art per state (UI kits): swaps the image instead of the default effect
quit_btn = SpriteButton("quit.png", hover="quit_hover.png", pressed="quit_down.png",
                    center=(400, 100), label="Quit", label_inset=(0, 0, 0, 6))

SpriteButton(source, center=, label=, font=, font_size=, label_color=, label_inset=, on_click=, enabled=, hover=, pressed=, disabled=, hover_sound=, click_sound=, hover_scale=, press_scale=, breathe=, breathe_time=, …)

Plus the Sprite parameters (width=, height=, size=, frame=, layer=, box=, …).

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning

label_colorname=color, Gradient or TexturewhiteColor of the label.
label_insetname=number or (left, top, right, bottom)0Margin of the label's box inside the art — for a border or a 3D "step" at the bottom. The label centers and fits in that box.

The press does not go through to what is under it (nor to mouse.press, as with any SpriteButton: the press belongs to the button); on_hover still runs. A function links it: enabled=lambda: st.coins >= 10 (or btn["enabled"] @= …).

hover_sound / click_soundname=file, Sound or NoneSound when the hover starts / on each click. The click sound keeps playing if the click calls change_act.
hover_scale / press_scalename=number1.06 / 0.94Drawn size on hover / when pressed. 1 turns it off. Only in the drawing: scale stays yours.

SpriteButton reference
PropertyTypeRead/WriteMeaning
labelstr or None"Play"read / writeThe text shown. Write a string or a number. To link it: btn.label_text["text"] @= lambda: ….
label_textText or NonereadThe label's Text, for fine control: font_size, set_color(Gradient(…)), glow. Its pose is relative to the center of the label's box (label_text.move_to(0, 4) raises it by 4). It moves, turns and disappears with the button; it has no layer or destroy() of its own.
label_inset(left, top, right, bottom)read / writeMargin of the label's box.

pointer_hover / pointer_pressedboolreadHovered / pressed right now (see Click / drag).

label is the string shortcut (as in Button); label_text is the object. The click area is the convex outline of the art at rest: transparent corners do not click, holes inside the art do, and the hover's growing/shrinking does not change the area. The effect is drawing only — btn.scale, width and the collision hitbox do not change.

Slider

A bar with a handle for picking a number within a range. Tied to a numeric Attribute: dragging writes the value, and changing the value moves the handle.

The range comes from min_value= / max_value= and the default is 0 to 100 — a volume from 0 to 1 needs max_value=1. slider.percentage reads the handle's position in the range, from 0 to 1. The mouse wheel over the Slider also changes the value: 1 per step with only_int=True, 2% of the range without it. The Slider does not correct the Attribute: a value already outside the range (or not an integer with only_int=True) stays as it is — the handle stops at the end — until a drag or the wheel writes a new value, always within the range.

st.volume = 0.5
st.lives = 3
Slider(st["volume"], label="Volume", max_value=1)
Slider(st["lives"], label="Lives", min_value=1, max_value=9, only_int=True)

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
cell1stfieldA numeric field. E.g. Slider(st["volume"], …).
labelname=str or NoneCaption to the left of the bar. Left out: the field's name (Slider(st["volume"]) shows st.volume).
min_value / max_valuename=number0 / 100The two ends of the bar. Equal, or a minimum above the maximum, raise ValueError.
initialname=number or NoneNoneStarting value; written to the Attribute. Without it and without an Attribute: the middle of the range.
only_intname=boolFalseTrue: the handle moves from integer to integer (lives, level).
show_valuename=boolTrueShows the current value to the right of the bar.

enabledname=boolTrueFalse: drawn dimmed and ignores clicks and keys (the click does not go through to the game; on_hover still fires). Also w.enabled = False. To hide it: visible = False.

CheckBox

A check box: it turns a boolean Attribute (True / False) on and off. Clicking flips the value; writing the value checks or unchecks the box. .checked is the value (True / False), like a Slider's .value: you can save it in JSON. The field is toggle["checked"] (to link it with @=).

st.mute = False
st.debug = False
CheckBox(st["mute"], label="Mute")
CheckBox(st["debug"], label="Colliders", initial=False)
Constructor

CheckBox(cell, label=, initial=, size=, enabled=)

Name without =: 1st, in order. Name with =: by name.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
cell1stfieldA bool field. E.g. CheckBox(st["mute"], …).
labelname=str"CheckBox"Caption to the right of the box.
initialname=boolFalseChecked or not at the start; written to the Attribute.
sizename=number18Side of the box, in design units. Left out: the theme's (18 × ui.scale).

TextInput

A one-line text box — the player's name, a seed, a console. Tied to a text or number Attribute: Enter, Tab or clicking outside write what was typed; Esc undoes the edit. While the box has the focus (the cursor blinking in it), the text keys belong to it, not to the game.

st.player_name = ""                  # st.name is reserved (it is the State's name)
st.seed = ""
TextInput(st["player_name"], placeholder="Name", label="Player", max_length=12)
TextInput(st["seed"], width=200, top_left=(20, 300))

def run(cmd):                        # console: Enter runs it and you keep typing
    print(cmd)
    console.text = ""
    console.focus()

console = TextInput(on_submit=run, width=400)
Constructor

TextInput(cell, placeholder=, label=, max_length=, on_submit=, width=, height=, initial=, top_left=, enabled=)

Name without =: 1st, in order. Name with =: by name.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
cell1stfieldA text or number field. The text is written to it on Enter, on Tab or when the box loses the focus. A bool field raises an error: use CheckBox. E.g. TextInput(st["player_name"], …).
placeholdername=str""Gray hint while the box is empty
labelname=str or NoneNoneCaption on the left. width includes the caption. When stacked, Sliders and TextInputs with a caption share the same caption column.
max_lengthname=int or NoneNoneMaximum number of characters when typing or pasting. A longer value set from code shows in full.
on_submitname=function or NoneRuns on Enter, after the text is written and the box loses the focus: fn() or fn(value) (the value already converted). It runs even when the text did not change; it does not run on a click outside, on Esc, or when the number does not convert. Also entry.on_submit = fn. To keep typing: entry.focus() inside the function.
initialname=str or numberNoneStarting text; written to the Attribute.
widthname=number260Width of the box, caption included, in design units. Left out: the theme's (260 × ui.scale).
heightname=number28Height, in design units. Left out: the theme's (28 × ui.scale).
enabledname=boolTrueFalse: dimmed, takes no focus, Tab skips it. Turning off a focused box writes its text.
.text—strThe text in the box right now — it may not be written to the field yet. When the field changes, the box shows the new value. Writing it changes what is shown; Enter or losing the focus writes it as if it were typed.
.is_valid—boolTrueRead-only. False when the last text written did not convert to the Attribute's type (e.g. "abc" in an int field); the field keeps its previous value, and the typed text stays in the box with an invalid background until you edit it, press Esc or the cell changes.
.focus()—methodGives the keyboard to the box, with its text selected (name screen, console). Raises an error if the box is hidden, turned off, destroyed, or a modal Menu is open.
.focused—boolRead-only. True while the box has the keyboard.

Keys: arrows, Home / End, Backspace / Del; Shift selects; Cmd (macOS) or Ctrl + A / C / X / V selects all and uses the clipboard; Option (macOS) or Ctrl + arrows / Backspace move by word. Dragging selects; a double click selects the word. Esc goes back to the field's value without writing and lets go of the focus. Tab / Shift+Tab go to the next / previous TextInput (in creation order). Text longer than the box scrolls.

Clicking in and leaving without editing never writes: 0.125 stays 0.125. While focused, keyp and on_key_* do not see the text and editing keys, nor Cmd/Ctrl + A / C / X / V / Z / Y (Z and Y do nothing: the box has no undo). Cmd/Ctrl + any other key, F1–F12 and Page Up / Down go through to the game, after the box writes its text as an Enter would, but the focus stays and on_submit does not run.

DropDown

A box that opens a list when clicked and lets you pick one option. Tied to an Attribute: the choice is written to it — the list item itself, not the text shown. dropdown.selected_index reads the position of the current option (0 = the first).

The list opens downward; near the bottom edge of the window, it opens upward. A list too long for the screen stops at the window's edge and scrolls with the mouse wheel (or two fingers on the trackpad); a small bar on the right shows where you are, and when it opens the current option appears in the middle. For a question that pauses the game, use Menu.

st.palette = "night"
st.weapon = "laser"
DropDown(st["palette"], options=["night", "sunset", "day"])
DropDown(st["weapon"], options=["laser", "rocket"], initial="laser")
Constructor

DropDown(cell, options=, initial=, width=, height=, enabled=)

Name without =: 1st, in order. Name with =: by name.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
cell1stfieldThe field for the selection. E.g. DropDown(st["palette"], …).
optionsname=list["night", "day"]The choices. The text shown is str() of each item. Without options=: three sample options ("Option 1"…). E.g. options=["night", "sunset", "day"].
initialname=an item of options"laser"Option selected at the start; written to the Attribute. Not in the list: the first one.
widthname=number260Width of the closed box, in design units. Left out: the theme's (260 × ui.scale).
heightname=number28Height, in design units. Left out: the theme's (28 × ui.scale).
enabledname=boolTrueFalse: drawn dimmed and ignores clicks and keys (the click does not go through to the game; on_hover still fires). Also w.enabled = False. To hide it: visible = False.
.text—strThe text of the current option, as it shows in the box. For reading only; the real choice is in the Attribute.

Menu

A Menu is a question in the middle of the window — pause, pick a ship, continue or quit. It appears when created; a click on an option picks it and closes the menu. Three ways to get the choice: an Attribute, the on_choose function, or await in an async mode. You pick with the mouse; it stays out of the widget column.

st.ship = "Blue"

def pick_ship(opt):
    pass

Menu(st["ship"], options=["Blue", "Red"], on_choose=pick_ship, title="Your ship")

async def pause_mode(e):
    answer = await Menu(options=["Continue", "Quit"], title="Paused", pause=True)

def update(dt):
    if keyp.once("ESC"):
        Menu(options=["Continue", "Title screen"], title="Paused", pause=True)
Constructor

Menu(cell, options=, on_choose=, title=, cols=1, modal=True, pause=False, center=, box=, font=, font_size=, color=, background=, icons=, group=)

options= is the only required one. cell is optional. center= and box= do not go together.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
cell1stfieldOptional. The field that gets the chosen option. E.g. Menu(st["ship"], …). None raises (it would be st.ship still empty, without brackets).
optionsname=list["Play", "Quit"]Choices. The label is str(). The chosen value is the item, not the text.
on_choosename=functionpick_shippick_ship(opt). Runs on every click, including the same option again. Does not run on destroy().
titlename=strBand at the top. Left out = only the options.
colsname=int1How many columns of options: 1 = a vertical list; len(options) = a single row; any other number = a grid.
modalname=boolTrueDarkens the game. Only one modal at a time; a second one raises an error naming the open one. False: no veil; a new one replaces the open one (the old one closes with None).
pausename=boolFalseTrue pauses the game (clock.paused) while the menu is open; on close, clock.paused goes back to what it was before. Works with modal=False.
centername=point or functionCenter on the window (view space), a value or a lambda. Followed every frame. The panel stays whole on the screen. It does not follow the camera.
boxname=BoxThe panel fills the box; the options are the size of their text, centered in it (a click on the panel outside them picks nothing). The font only shrinks if it does not fit, down to a readable minimum; below that it cuts and warns.
font / font_sizename=str / number"pixel.ttf"A family or a .ttf / .otf file. Leaving out font uses ui.font.
colorname=color"white"Color of the labels. When it is given, the highlight of the option under the mouse comes from this color.
backgroundname=color, Gradient or TextureGradient("red", "gold")Panel background. Gradient and Texture fit the panel as in a shape's fill: the gradient runs to the panel's edge, and the Gradient's size= is measured from the panel's center. The title band is a little lighter. Without color, the highlight of the option under the mouse comes from the background (the Gradient's mean_color(), the Texture's color). An animated fill (WaterFill …) or a value that is not a color raises an error at creation.
iconsname=list of filesOne image per option, above the label. The chosen value is still the option. A number of icons different from the number of options raises an error. A missing file: a checkerboard and a warning.
Menu reference
TopicRule
On choosingCloses, gives back the pause, writes the Attribute, completes the await, destroys itself, then calls on_choose.
await menuThe choice, or None if it closed without a choice. Never Cancelled. It does not need await. Leaving the mode destroys the menu.
destroy()Closes with no choice. Whoever is waiting gets None. on_choose does not run. .choice is read-only.
KeysWith a modal, keyp / mouse.press read false. The click that picks stays hidden until the button is released. Open the pause with keyp.once("ESC") — a key held during the menu does not count as a new press when it closes.
WhereWithout center / box: the size of its text, at the center of the view (not the HUD column). center=lambda: hero.center only follows the hero if the camera does not move.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
DropDownMenu closes on choosing and blocks the game. DropDown stays in the column and does not pause.the same widget
A Button for each optionMenu is a single question. Several buttons stay on the screen.a menu

ui.gap

ui.gap() opens an extra space between the last item in the column and the next one. Each call adds one space; nothing is drawn.

st.volume = 0.5
st.palette = "night"
Text("Volume")
Slider(st["volume"], label="Volume", max_value=1)
ui.gap()
Button(label="Reset", on_click=reset)

ui.gap()
ui.gap()
DropDown(st["palette"], options=["night", "day"])
Call

ui.gap()

No arguments. No object. The extra space is the same as the theme's space between items (12 at ui.scale=1).

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
ui.gap()No parameters—Adds one extra space. The normal space between items stays.
Applies to——The next HUD Text or widget created without top_left=.
Empty column——The 1st item ignores the gap; it is kept for the 2nd.

ui.stack_reset / stack_origin / stack_from / stack_column clear pending gaps. An item with an explicit top_left= does not use them up. It is not a Box. See Column.

ui.stack_column

ui.stack_column() makes the next item start a new column, to the right of the current one and level with its top. Nothing is drawn.

st.volume = 0.5
st.pan = 0.0
st.mute = False
Slider(st["volume"], label="Volume", max_value=1)
Slider(st["pan"], label="Pan", min_value=-1, max_value=1)

ui.stack_column()
CheckBox(st["mute"], label="Mute")
Button(label="Reset", on_click=reset)

ui.stack_column(gap=24)
Text("One more")
Call

ui.stack_column() · ui.stack_column(gap=24)

The new x is the right edge of the widest item in the column, plus the space. The new y is the visual top of this column. Without gap=, the space is the theme's (12 at ui.scale=1).

MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
ui.stack_column()Parameters: gap= (number, optional)—The next item created without top_left= starts another column to the right, at the same top.
gap=number—Horizontal space. Left out: the same theme space as between items.
Column width——Up to the right edge of the widest item that took a place in the column (HUD Text and widgets). Not the last item.
Empty column——Advances by the default widget width + the space. Two calls in a row skip an empty column.
Applies to——The next HUD Text or widget created without top_left=.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
ui.stack_column() goes to a fixed point on the screenui.stack_column() takes x and y from the column it just built: x to the right of it, y at its top. It clears a pending ui.gap (the vertical gap does not become space between columns). The labels of the Sliders in the new column line up with each other, not with those of the previous column.an absolute point — that is ui.stack_origin(x, y)

Utilities

Small calculations that show up in every game: convert a value from one range to another (remap), blend two values (lerp), chase a target smoothly (chase) or at constant speed (approach), give a camera some slack (deadzone) and roll yes or no (chance). Math with points and vectors: Geometry.

Remap a range → remap
Blend two values → lerp
Chase with a lag → chase
Chase at constant speed → approach
Camera slack → deadzone
Yes/no → chance

remap

Takes a value from one range to another. Optional: a curve in between (modifier=).

x = remap(hp, 0, 100, 8, 40)
# hp 0 → 8 · hp 100 → 40 · hp 50 → 24

x = remap(hp, 0, 100, 8, 40, modifier="ease_in")
# normalize → curve → output; without modifier= it is linear
Signature

remap(value, in_min=0, in_max=1, out_min=0, out_max=1, modifier=None)

Parameters: value, in_min, in_max, out_min, out_max (numbers); modifier (name or function). Returns a number.

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
value1stnumber0.5Input value.
in_min, in_max2nd, 3rdnumber (0, 1)0, 100Input range. in_min == in_max returns out_min.
out_min, out_max4th, 5thnumber (0, 1)0, 255Output range.
modifier=name=name or function"ease_in"A curve on [0,1]→[0,1], applied after normalizing. Without it: linear. The same names as ease=, plus spring · wobble (only here: they start and end at 0.5, so they swing around the middle of the output range). Or a callable. An unknown name → ValueError with the list.

Pipeline: normalizes value to [0,1] with in_min…in_max → applies modifier → scales to out_min…out_max.

Curves like bounce / elastic / spring can go outside [out_min, out_max] or not be monotonic. For a custom curve: modifier=lambda t: ….

lerp

Interpolates between two values of the same type. A number, a flat tuple/list of numbers, Vec2, Color, or two Points (returns (x, y)). t is not clamped — eases like elastic go past 0–1.

lerp(0, 100, 0.5)                        # 50
lerp((0, 0), (100, 40), 0.25)             # (25.0, 10.0)
lerp(Color("red"), Color("blue"), 0.5)    # blends in OKLAB
lerp(ship.center, target.center, 0.5)     # (x, y) — does not create a Point
Signature

lerp(a, b, t)

Parameters: a, b (same type / shape); t (number). Returns the same type as a (or (x, y) for Point).

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
a, b1st, 2ndsame typeColor("red")The two ends. Number · tuple/list · Vec2 · Color · Point.
t3rdnumber0.5How far to go from a to b: 0 = a, 1 = b, 0.5 = halfway. Values outside 0–1 are not cut off (they go past a or b).

It is the same math tween uses to animate a field. Tuples and lists work only if they are flat: numbers, not tuples inside tuples.

Mismatched types or lengths raise an error right away. Not in the middle of the animation. lerp on two Points returns a tuple, not a new Point (a Point is a game object).

chase

chase brings a value closer to a target, a little each frame: fast when it is far and slow when it is close, without going past the target — and at the same pace at any frame rate. Good for a camera that follows, or an HP bar that drops smoothly. It takes the same types as lerp.

bar.width = chase(bar.width, hp, rate=8.0)
look = chase((canvas.pan_x, canvas.pan_y), hero.center, rate=6.0)
canvas.pan_to(look)
Signature

chase(current, target, rate, dt=None)

Parameters: current, target (same type / shape); rate (number); dt (number, optional). Returns the same type as lerp(current, target, t).

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
current, target1st, 2ndsame type(100, 80)The two ends. Number · tuple · Vec2 · Color · Point (returns (x, y)).
rate3rdnumber6How fast it closes in, per second: every 1/rate of a second, the remaining distance drops to about a third. With rate=6, it has covered ~95% of the way in 0.5 s. Higher = gets there sooner.
dt4th or name=numberclock.dtOptional. Left out = the world's step (clock.dt). Pass dt= in on_update if the Entity has a time_scale, or for a step you compute yourself. dt == 0 (game paused) or rate == 0 returns current without changing anything; a negative dt or rate → ValueError.

It is lerp(current, target, 1 - exp(-rate * dt)). You call it in update. It does not register anything, does not keep running afterwards, does not compete with a tween. Camera recipe: Camera.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
canvas.follow(hero) makes the camera followa verb that does not exist. Following is chase + pan_to every frame. pan_to(..., time=) (or speed=) freezes the destination at the moment of the call.pan_to(..., time=) alone
chase always moves at the same speeda slowdown: it brakes near the target and, in theory, never arrives exactly. Constant speed and an exact arrival is approach.approach

approach

approach goes from current to target always at the same speed, speed units per second, and arrives exactly: when one step or less is left, it returns the target itself. Called every frame with a moving target, it chases at constant speed. It is the sibling of chase, which slows down as it arrives.

enemy.move_to(approach(enemy.center, player.center, 120))
bar.width = approach(bar.width, hp * 2, 80)

pos = approach(elevator.center, (400, 120), 90)
elevator.move_to(pos)
if pos == (400, 120):
    print("arrived")
Signature

approach(current, target, speed, dt=None)

Parameters: current, target (two numbers or two points); speed (number); dt (number, optional). Returns a number, a Vec2 (if current is a Vec2) or (x, y).

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
current, target1st, 2ndnumber or pointhero.centerWhere from and where to. Two numbers, or two points: Point, Vec2, (x, y), mouse or a shape's .center. Color → TypeError (use chase).
speed3rdnumber120Speed, in units per second. Each call moves speed * dt. Negative → ValueError.
dt4th or name=numberclock.dtOptional. Left out = the world's step (clock.dt, the same dt that update(dt) receives). Pass dt= in on_update if the Entity has a time_scale. dt == 0 (game paused) or speed == 0 returns current; a negative dt → ValueError.

A point moves in a straight line to the target; on a diagonal, at the same speed as on the horizontal. It never goes past the target or jitters around it, and the arrival is exact: the returned value equals the target (you can test it with ==, as in pos == (400, 120)), and move_to(pos) puts the center exactly there. Compare the returned value, not elevator.center == (400, 120): a Point is never equal to a tuple. You call it in update. It does not register anything, does not keep running afterwards, does not compete with a tween. It pairs with deadzone for a pet on a leash.

Pass the whole point, not x and y separately. approach(ball.center.x, mouse.x, 300) plus another call for y makes the diagonal move faster (√2 times) and reaches one axis before the other. With chase, splitting the axes gives the same result; with approach, it does not. Angles do not take the short way around either: from 350 to 10, approach goes through 180.

Don't confuse

Looks likeIt isIt is not
approach and chase do the same thingtwo different motions: chase brakes near the target and does not arrive exactly; approach moves at constant speed and arrives exactly.two spellings of the same math
move_to(target, time=2) chasesa one-time read: time= (and speed= too) reads the destination once, at the call. To follow a moving target, approach in update, every frame.move_to(..., time=)

deadzone

deadzone lets the target move freely inside a box of size size around current; only when the target leaves the box does the result move, just enough to bring it back to the box's border. For a camera that does not shake with every step the hero takes.

look = (canvas.pan_x, canvas.pan_y)
tx, ty = deadzone(look, hero.center, size=(160, 90))
if hero.grounded:
    ty = canvas.pan_y          # lock Y on the ground — a platformer rule, written by you
canvas.pan_to(chase(look, (tx, ty), rate=6.0))
Signature

deadzone(current, target, size)

Parameters: current, target (point); size (number or pair). Returns (x, y).

ParameterPassType (default)Meaning
current, target1st, 2ndpointhero.centerPoint, Vec2, (x, y) or Graphic (its center).
size3rdnumber or pair(160, 90)Full width and height of the box, in design units, centered on current (size=160 → 80 on each side). A number = a square (160 ≡ (160, 160)). float("inf") on an axis locks that axis (the result stays at current).

Pairs with chase for a camera with slack. It also works outside the camera (aiming, a pet on a leash). An invalid size → TypeError.

Inside the box the result is current. It does not wobble at rest. Rules like “do not follow y while the hero is on the ground” (common in platformers) go in an if of your own, not inside deadzone.

chance

chance(p) rolls the dice: it returns True with probability p, from 0 to 1. chance(0.30) is true 30% of the time.

if chance(0.30):
    drop_loot()
Signature

chance(p)

Parameters: p (number 0 to 1). Returns True/False.

TopicRule
p0 to 1. 0 never, 1 always. Anything else → error.
UseOne roll. It is not an interval — for a steady rhythm use ready.

chance in update rolls every frame. 0.30 at 60 fps ≈ 18 times per second. A steady rhythm: ready. A number in a range: from random import uniform.

Debug

Debugging tools for a running game — overlay methods and keyboard shortcuts — and the catalog of the exceptions Scena raises. The tools are not game-logic API — nothing here takes part in @collide, resolve or the outcome of the game.

show_colliders / show_tracks / show_processes → Methods
HUD / overlay / pause / fullscreen → Keyboard shortcuts
Exception → cause → fix → Error catalog

Methods

Functions that only draw debug overlays on top of the screen. No effect at all on collision, physics or game logic.

collision.show_colliders(enabled=True)
show_tracks(enabled=True)
show_processes(enabled=True)
Debug reference
MethodSignatureReturnsMeaning
collision.show_colliders(enabled=True)Parameters: enabled (on, True/False)—Draws the registered hitboxes (gold = resolve; cyan = an add_hitbox part; green = detection only). The rectangle of a moving object (gold) and its parts (cyan) show together. Ctrl+Shift+7. Queries: Queries. What enters the system: What collides.
show_tracks(enabled=True)Parameters: enabled (on, True/False)—Magenta overlay of the active move_along trips and of the Tracks sitting on a layer. It does not turn on Track.visible. Also collision.show_tracks (same method, another name). Ctrl+Shift+7 (the inspection zoom of Ctrl+Shift+8 does not show the tracks). Off: no extra work in the frame. See Track.
show_processes(enabled=True)Parameters: enabled (on, True/False)—A panel in the top right corner with what is running. One line per task (run_task, the body of an async mode): owner (the class; act / game with no owner; (parked) / (time 0) when the owner is stopped), function, kind, age, what it waits for (wait 0.3s left, move_to 0.6s left, until 4.1s, parallel 1/3 done, race of 3), the line of the await (inside a helper function too) and how much work it owns (+2 work). A task started by another one is indented under it. Then one line per mode (sync = def; with mode_time and the mode's timers). Identical lines become one: Wasp x12. A wait of 5 s or more in an until / until_empty (or a race / parallel with no clock) turns amber, SLOW — only in the panel, never a warning: waiting for a key on the title screen is normal. Ctrl+Shift+6 (the second press also shows the loose timers). Off: no extra work in the frame. See tasks.

Keyboard shortcuts

Shortcuts that work in any Scena game while it runs: all of them are Ctrl+Shift + a digit or letter, on Mac and PC (the F1–F7 keys usually belong to the system).

ShortcutWhat it does
Ctrl+Shift+1Turns the system HUD on / off (FPS, objs, mouse xy in the world; with tasks running, how many and how many are slow: tasks: 3 (1 slow)). Starts off.
Ctrl+Shift+2Turns automatic quality adjustment (FX Auto) on / off: when the game does not fit in the frame, Scena lowers the quality of the effects (high → medium → low) and, last, the rate (60 → 30 fps); if the game logic is what weighs, it goes straight to 30 and keeps the quality. Starts on, at high and 60 fps.
Ctrl+Shift+3Cycles the render profile: low → medium → high.
Ctrl+Shift+4Cycles the framerate: vsync → vsync60 → vsync30 → 60 → 30 → max.
Ctrl+Shift+6Process panel: off → tasks and modes → also the loose timers (every / after / sounds outside any mode or task) → off. The same panel: show_processes(enabled=True).
Ctrl+Shift+7Overlay: colliders + design frame + origin cross + move_along tracks. With @leave_playfield, the playfield too. The same drawing: collision.show_colliders(enabled=True) / show_tracks(enabled=True).
Ctrl+Shift+8Inspection zoom: 100% → 50% → 25%. Does not change canvas.zoom. Design frame / playfield; no tracks.
Ctrl+Shift+ECloses the SCENA WARNING banner (the badge above the FPS; e.g. a missing sound). An error in your code does not become a banner: it comes up with the traceback.
Ctrl+Shift+PTime: running → paused → ¼ → running. Gives back the script's clock.scale when the cycle completes.
Ctrl+Shift+FFullscreen: covers the monitor (no border, no taskbar). Keeps the aspect with black bars. If the window was maximized, pressing F again leaves fullscreen and goes back to maximized. The same as canvas.display = "fullscreen" (the shortcut toggles).
Ctrl+Shift+MMaximizes on the desktop (the taskbar stays). Content with black bars. The title bar's Maximize button is the same mode. From fullscreen, M leaves F and maximizes. The same as canvas.display = "maximized" (the shortcut toggles).
Ctrl+Shift+ZQuits.

Ctrl+Shift+5 does nothing. A Shape's drag handles show with shape.show_handles() — it is per object, there is no global shortcut. M and F toggle; in the script use canvas.display = … (absolute). There is no toggle_fullscreen().

Error catalog

When a use is wrong, Scena raises one of these exceptions. The name tells the cause; the message shows the spelling that works.

ExceptionTypical causeFix
CallableAssignErrorobj.field = lambda or st.x = lambdaship["hp"] @= lambda: …
LinkedAttributeErrorWriting a field that already has @=.unlink() first, or write on the other side of the formula
DerivedAttributeErrorWriting a derived (read-only) fieldWrite the field that defines it (center, not a computed corner). To put a computed point in a place, move the object by it: r.move_to(1, 2, about=r.top_right). The error message says what the field is computed from and shows the right form.
DestroyedErrorA change to an object that was already destroyed (move_by, rotate_by, visible, layer, tag, own field, radius =)if ship: before the call. Reading still works: .center and own fields (enemy.value) still read; only changing raises. destroy() again does nothing. move_by(..., time=), after and play_sound return an already cancelled Handle, silently (the sound does not play)
CircularReferenceErrorAn @= that closes a loop: a["radius"] @= lambda: b.radius and then b["radius"] @= lambda: a.radiusLink one direction only; the other side gets = (or is written in update(dt)). The message names both ends
ParallaxLayerErrorclickable / draggable / collision on an object of a parallax layer (pan_response ≠ 1 …)Parallax layers are decoration only. Put the playable object on a layer without parallax. It raises when you name the object (@collide(coin, …), coin.clickable = True); a group member on that layer (@collide("hero", "coin")) is left out of the rule, with a warning. It is also a ValueError
UiLayerErrorCollision or SpatialFx on the "ui" layer"ui" is screen space (HUD). Use a world layer. It is also a ValueError
ActUsageErrorTreating an Act as a game object: self.visible, self.layer, @collide_with in an actThe act does not draw or collide; the rule goes in the object's class, or @collide(a, b) inside setup(). It is also a TypeError / AttributeError
CancelledAn await on a Handle that was cancelled (async wait, tasks)Not your error: the mode or the task ended. try / finally to clean up. It is a BaseException — except Exception does not catch it
TypeErrorWrong type: a string where a number goes, bool, Circle(10); wrong parameter name (Polygon(pionts=…))The message names the parameter and gives an example (Circle(center=(0, 0), radius=10)), or Did you mean 'points'? + the Valid: list
TypeErrorAn st field without brackets where it is linked or watched: Slider(st.volume), Text(st.score), @on_change(st.lives), tween(st.t, …), until(st.over), c["radius"] @= st.rst.volume is the value; the field is st["volume"] (since 0.8.0). The message shows the spelling with brackets
TypeErrorBrackets inside a lambda or used as a number: Text(lambda: f"Score: {st['score']}"), c["radius"] @= lambda: st["r"] * 2, @when(lambda: st["lives"] == 0), if st["alive"]:Inside the lambda, a dot: st.score. The lambda already keeps the sum live; st["score"] is the field, not the number. The message shows the spelling with a dot
TypeErrorAt the class line: a method Scena would never call. A method named update in a class, with any signature (even a helper def update(self): update belongs to Scena) (the every-frame hook is on_update; in a shape, update is the internal recompute of linked fields); on_key_down / on_mouse_click / … (top-of-file names) in an act or an object; a name one letter away from a hook (on_colide, on_updat, on_destory) or another engine's on_collision (the Unity and Godot hooks, Update, Start, OnTriggerEnter2D, _process, give a SCENA WARNING with Scena's name); a method named collide_with. If the class has several, the message lists them all, each with its lineThe message says the right name: on_update(self, dt); in an act, keyp.once("SPACE") / mouse.press() in on_update; in an object, on_click(self); Did you mean on_collide?. A helper of your own (on_hit, on_frame) passes: only names one letter away from a hook are refused
AttributeErrorWriting a name the type does not have: a Scena field of another type (rect.text = …), another engine's spelling (x.position = …), or a name one letter away from a short property, with a value of its type (ball.colr = "red", ball.angl = 45)The message says the right name (Scena spells it 'center', Did you mean 'color'?); a field of your own needs another name
ValueErrorA number outside the domain: negative size, NaN, a layer that does not existThe message gives the range or Did you mean

Problems that do not stop the game — a missing sound or image file, an unknown color name — become a SCENA WARNING, not an exception: the game goes on (silence, a checkerboard in place of the image; a color name that is almost right becomes the nearest color, an unknown name becomes magenta) and an amber banner in the corner shows the warning. Ctrl+Shift+E closes the banner. Two warnings are about the game, not about an error: “mode … frozen for 2s with nothing pending” comes when a mode sits still with nothing to do (no timer, no task, no on_update); if it only waits for a click or has already finished its work, that is fine (to leave the mode, self.mode = None). “leak-detector: objects rising” comes when the number of objects rises without stopping; in a game where the population grows on purpose (bigger and bigger waves), just check that the objects that leave are destroyed.
